subzone:bal-lal-ruins.text: Bal'lal Ruins. Bal'lal Ruins are ancient Gurubashi troll ruins set along the northwestern shore of Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Overlooking the murky waters of the Vile Reef, the crumbling stone foundations are currently occupied by hostile Bloodscalp trolls. Perched on the coastline north of Grom'gol Base Camp, Bal'lal Ruins stand as another remnant of the shattered Gurubashi Empire. Once part of the grand troll civilization that dominated southern Azeroth, the site has decayed into moss-covered stone walls and cracked masonry. The ruins sit immediately adjacent to the Vile Reef, offering an elevated vantage over the treacherous coastal shallows. Today, aggressive Bloodscalp trolls hold the grounds, fiercely defending the weathered relics of their ancestors against intruders.

subzone:balia-mah-ruins.text: Balia'mah Ruins. The Balia'mah Ruins are the moss-covered remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Located east of Grom'gol Base Camp across the river, the crumbling stone tiers are currently claimed and guarded by warriors of the hostile Skullsplitter troll tribe. Like many of the stone edifices dotting the jungle, Balia'mah stands as a remnant of the sprawling Gurubashi Empire that once ruled much of the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Following the fall of their ancient capital, Gurubashi territory splintered into warring factions. Today, the ruins serve as a stronghold for the Skullsplitter tribe, who fiercely defend the stone terraces against wandering beasts, neighboring ogres from the Mosh'Ogg mound, and any outsiders foolish enough to cross the river.

subzone:bay-of-storms.text: Bay of Storms. The Bay of Storms is an expansive, tempestuous gulf carving into the rugged eastern cliffs of Azshara. Its churning waters harbor ancient ruins, submerged caverns, and perilous marine beasts that make seafaring along this coast hazardous. Opening out toward the Great Sea, the Bay of Storms defines much of Azshara's dramatic coastal geography. Far from a tranquil harbor, its turbulent waters and rocky outcrops are home to dangerous wildlife and ancient aquatic threats. Within and along its waters lie landmarks like the sunken Temple of Arkkoran, the coral reefs of Hetaera's Clutch, and Scalebeard's Cave, leaving the bay largely avoided by casual sailors and claimed instead by coastal monsters.

subzone:bear-s-head.text: Bear's Head. Bear's Head is a secluded mountainous stretch along the southeastern cliffs of Azshara. Named for the resident Timbermaw furbolgs whose settlements dot the rugged high ground, it serves as an outpost linked to their larger homes farther north while lying directly beneath the cliffside sanctum of Archmage Xylem. Tucked away in southeastern Azshara, Bear's Head takes its name from the encampments of uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs established upon its heights. These rustic settlements act as outlying camps tied to the major furbolg dens of Ursolan and Timbermaw Hold to the north. Perched atop the looming cliffs directly above the area sits Xylem's Tower, an eccentric sanctuary where Archmage Xylem and his small retinue of apprentices conduct arcane studies in quiet isolation from the rest of the troubled coastline.

subzone:beezil-s-wreck.text: Beezil's Wreck. Beezil's Wreck marks the crash site of an unfortunate goblin zeppelin deep within the quagmires of Dustwallow Marsh. Resting east of Tabetha's Farm, the shattered vessel's cargo holds scattered supplies and volatile engineering components that attract scavengers. Hidden away in the humid muck east of Tabetha's Farm lies the splintered skeleton of a goblin zeppelin known as Beezil's Wreck. The craft was hauling cargo southward across Kalimdor before suffering a disastrous plunge into the swamp. While the wreckage still smolders amid tangled reeds, its eccentric captain, Beezil, has seemingly vanished from the marsh, leaving behind scattered crates and ticking machinery to slowly rot in the brine. Despite the harsh environment, the crash site remains a prime target for opportunistic explorers. The airship carried a payload of volatile goods, notably Seaforium boosters and heavy crates that survived the impact. Scavengers daring enough to wade through the surrounding beasts often risk life and limb to secure what is left of the lost shipment before corrosive marsh water ruins the haul entirely.

subzone:bitter-reaches.text: Bitter Reaches. The Bitter Reaches is a rugged, windswept wilderness in northeastern Azshara. Largely untouched by civilization, the rugged cliffs are prowled by predatory beasts and massive mountain giants. Occupying the northeastern cliffs of Azshara, the Bitter Reaches remains a stark and untamed stretch of rocky terrain overlooking the Great Sea. Flocks of feral hippogryphs and two-headed chimaeras nest amidst the heights, while acidic oozes seep through the cold ground. Along the high northern ridges, colossal mountain giants have claimed the slopes as their own, driving away lesser creatures and turning the frozen approaches into a perilous hazard for any solitary traveler. Despite the harsh winds and aggressive predators, the craggy landscape sustains rare mountain flora. Sparse clusters of Mountain Silversage cling to the high rock faces and windy perches, making the dangerous terrain occasionally worth traversing for intrepid herbalists daring enough to avoid the giants and territorial chimaeras.

subzone:black-channel-marsh.text: Black Channel Marsh. Black Channel Marsh is a murky mire situated in the southwestern Wetlands, flanking the main road leading toward Menethil Harbor. Infested with aggressive raptors, the soggy terrain poses an immediate threat to unwary travelers and supply couriers traversing the coastal lowlands. Stretching across the swampy low ground southwest of the main thoroughfare, Black Channel Marsh is infamous among caravan drivers and couriers heading to Menethil Harbor. While the raised road offers the illusion of safety, the stagnant channels and thick reeds are home to territorial raptor packs. Hungry beasts frequently stray directly into traffic, ambushing fresh recruits and weary wayfarers who stray even a pace or two from the beaten path.

subzone:blackchar-cave.text: Blackchar Cave. Blackchar Cave is a mysterious, sealed-off cavern tucked into the southwestern crags of Searing Gorge, close to the base of Blackrock Mountain. Its entrance is choked with impassable rubble and rock. Tucked away against the scorching crags near the approaches to Blackrock Mountain, Blackchar Cave presents a solid wall of stone where a deep cavern entrance might once have been. Heavy rubble and scorched slag choke the opening, preventing anyone from exploring whatever tunnels lie deeper within the mountain roots. The desolate terrain around it is scorched by ash and magma, offering little comfort to wanderers.

subzone:bloodfen-burrow.text: Bloodfen Burrow. Bloodfen Burrow is a cavern in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with vicious raptors. The beasts have claimed the cave and the surrounding clearing, completely overrunning the ruins of a settlement that once tried to survive the wetlands. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Bloodfen Burrow serves as the primary den for the region's aggressive Bloodfen raptors. The cave mouth and surrounding hollow crawl with the pack, drawn to the sheltered crevice and the bountiful hunting ground the marsh provides. Just outside the entrance lie scattered debris and splintered remains of an unidentified settlement, serving as a grim reminder of who truly rules the swamp's interior. Travelers also whisper that Cortello, an adventurous buccaneer, left one of his hidden riddle clues somewhere within this deadly den.

subzone:bloodvenom-falls.text: Bloodvenom Falls. Bloodvenom Falls is a towering, foul waterfall plunging down the corrupted cliffs of northern Felwood. Its toxic flow feeds the Bloodvenom River, spreading demon-spawned rot down the mountains and into downstream lands. Pouring over the bluffs in Felwood, Bloodvenom Falls represents one of the most vivid wounds inflicted upon the ancient forests of Kalimdor. Once a pristine mountain cascade, the waters were warped into a virulent sludge during the Third War by demonic magics and the remnants of the Burning Legion. The falls feed directly into the Bloodvenom River, which weaves through the heart of Felwood. From there, the tainted torrent rushes down the mountain slopes to become the foul Wildbend River in Darkshore, carrying blight far beyond Felwood's blighted borders. The virulent runoff from Bloodvenom Falls does not merely discolor the riverbed; it warps everything it touches. The swampy banks surrounding its spray breed twisted treants, sickening beasts, and aggressive slimes. For druids and wardens attempting to contain Felwood's rot, the falls are a chilling reminder that northern Kalimdor's waters remain deeply sickened at their source.

subzone:bloodvenom-post.text: Bloodvenom Post. Bloodvenom Post is a remote Horde settlement perched on the rocky bluffs of western Felwood overlooking Darkshore. Its tauren-style structures and tauren guards provide a foothold in a region infested with demonic taint and corrupted wildlife. Tucked away along the high cliffs above Darkshore, Bloodvenom Post is reached by following the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River away from Felwood's main thoroughfare. Built with traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts, this encampment provides Horde wanderers with a vital base of operations amidst a dying forest. From here, scouts track the encroaching demonic forces, study the spreading corruption of the waters, and attempt to monitor the hostile wildlife mutated by the Burning Legion's lingering power. Beyond observing the tainted wilds of Felwood, the camp sits right upon the precipice peering down over northern Darkshore. Its isolated position serves a double duty: keeping Horde forces informed of night elf movements along the western coastline while remaining well out of easy reach of Alliance patrols traversing the forest's central road.

subzone:bloodvenom-river.text: Bloodvenom River. The Bloodvenom River is a foul waterway cutting through central Felwood, saturated with the demonic corruption that blighted the ancient forest. Its putrid waters seep downstream across the mountains into Darkshore, transforming into the tainted Wildbend River. Running through the corrupted heart of Felwood, the Bloodvenom River serves as an open conduit of the land's spiritual and physical decay. Its banks are thick with vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul run-off left in the wake of the Burning Legion's invasion. The corruption within the channel is potent enough to taint lands far beyond Felwood itself, flowing westward down into the coastal forests of Darkshore as the Wildbend River.

subzone:bluegill-marsh.text: Bluegill Marsh. Bluegill Marsh is a sodden mire in the western Wetlands that serves as the sprawling settlement for the hostile Bluegill murloc tribe. The waterways and huts are fiercely guarded by these aquatic humanoids under the rule of the brute known as Gobbler. Travelers heading through the western fens must navigate carefully to avoid being surrounded in the shallows. Situated amidst the boggy flats of the western Wetlands, Bluegill Marsh is thick with mud, reeds, and the squawking war cries of its resident murlocs. The Bluegill tribe has erected crude primitive camps throughout the stagnant water, claiming this territory as their own. Unlike more isolated beasts of the swamp, these murlocs live and hunt in tightly knit packs. Wary wanderers and scouts from Menethil Harbor know that wading into their territory invites swift ambushes from every direction, especially with the formidable chieftain Gobbler prowling the murky shallows.

subzone:bolgan-s-hole.text: Bolgan's Hole. Bolgan's Hole is a subterranean cavern nestled in the southern cliffs of Gelkis Village in Desolace. It serves as the inner sanctum of the Gelkis centaur clan, housing their highest chieftains and sacred earth relics. Carved deep into the craggy bluffs overlooking the Gelkis encampment, Bolgan's Hole functions as the command center for the tribe. It is here that the ruling khan holds court, surrounded by veteran guards and the tribe's most influential shamans. The cavern offers natural fortification against rival clans, most notably the bloodthirsty Magram centaur to the east. Beyond its military importance, the cave possesses profound religious significance to the Gelkis. Luminous blue mineral formations known as the tears of Theradras sprout from the damp stone walls. Gelkis shamans obsessively harvest and guard these crystals, revering them as divine blessings that confer the subterranean protection of Princess Theradras, the primal earth elemental mother of the centaur race.

subzone:boulder-gor.text: Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor is a rugged hill in the western Arathi Highlands, situated directly north of the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. It serves as an active encampment for the Boulderfist ogres and their unusual allies among the Witherbark forest trolls. Rising just north of the crumbling ramparts of Stromgarde Keep, Boulder'gor is a steep bluff claimed by the Boulderfist clan. Within its shadows sits the Boulderfist Outpost mound, making it a central bastion of ogre power across the highlands. Uniquely, the ogres here share their fires and fortifications with forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe, including shadowy spellcasters who lend their dark magic to the clan's brute force. This mutual cooperation poses an ongoing danger to any travelers passing along the central roads of Arathi. The slopes around Boulder'gor look down over the open highlands of western Arathi. Hemmed between the Syndicate-infiltrated ruins of Stromgarde and the wild elemental sites of the plains, Boulder'gor remains a heavily guarded and hostile stronghold of tribal solidarity against both Alliance and Horde wanderers.

subzone:boulderfist-hall.text: Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist Hall is a heavily fortified ogre mound nestled in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just north of Thandol Span. It serves as the local stronghold for the Boulderfist ogres, who exert their brute influence across the neighboring trade routes and valleys under the command of Kor'gresh Coldrage. Carved into the rugged southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands, Boulderfist Hall is the principal redoubt of the Boulderfist clan in the region. Sheltered within its earthen ramparts and deep caverns, ogre brutes and magi maintain a fortified settlement mere steps from Witherbark Village and the strategic bridge at Thandol Span. Deep within the mound lurks their regional chieftain, Kor'gresh Coldrage, alongside enforcers like Phalanax. From this stronghold, the ogres project violent control over the surrounding roads, making any peaceful transit between Arathi and the Wetlands perilous for travelers and supply caravans alike.

subzone:boulderfist-outpost.text: Boulderfist Outpost. Boulderfist Outpost is a fortified mound nestled deep within the ogre settlement of Boulder'gor in the Arathi Highlands. Serving as an interior den and holding area, it houses aggressive Boulderfist ogres alongside a few Witherbark trolls. Carved into the earth and stone of western Arathi, Boulderfist Outpost functions as the heart of Boulder'gor. While brute enforcers dominate the settlement above, the outpost's interior concentrates the clan's core strength and provides a dark subterranean shelter. A handful of Witherbark troll witch doctors occasionally mingle among the ogres here, hinting at tenuous tribal cooperation.

subzone:brackenwall-village.text: Brackenwall Village. Brackenwall Village is the primary Horde outpost in Dustwallow Marsh, nestled among the bogs in the northwest corner of the zone. Founded by surviving Stonemaul ogres after dragons devastated their original settlement to the south, the village serves as a tenuous stronghold surrounded by Alliance spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight. When black dragonkin drove the Stonemaul ogres out of their ancient home at Stonemaul Village in the southern marsh, their leader, Overlord Mok'Morokk—successor to Rexxar—led the survivors north into the swamp to build Brackenwall. Formed around traditional earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower, the settlement gave the battered clan a defensible haven. Though aligned with the Horde, the village suffers from internal rot: Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoarding supplies and refusing to confront the draconic threat, leaving the clan's spiritual and tactical guidance to figures like the ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries.

subzone:broken-hall.text: Broken Hall. The Broken Hall serves as the flooded outer threshold of the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Shattered when the Great Dragon Aspect Ysera and her flight dragged the grand ziggurat beneath the waters, this ruin now stands deserted as the Atal'ai zealots retreat into deeper sanctums. When the green dragons brought down their wrath upon the Atal'ai priesthood and submerged their unholy ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outermost architecture bore the brunt of the cataclysm. The floor of the Broken Hall collapsed completely, allowing murky swamp waters to flood the chamber. Because of the damage and submersion, the troll cultists abandoned this entrance hall, withdrawing further into the complex. Adventurers entering the sunken temple must wade through these sodden ruins before mounting the stairs to reach the Hall of Masks.

subzone:broken-pillar.text: Broken Pillar. The Broken Pillar is a weathered cluster of ancient troll ruins jutting from the dunes south of Gadgetzan. It serves as an isolated research post for the goblin prospector and scientist Marvon Rivetseeker, who studies the enigmatic artifacts buried beneath the surrounding sands. Rising out of the sands south of Gadgetzan and east of the treacherous Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar marks the remnants of ancient troll architecture long swallowed by Tanaris. Despite the desolate surroundings and encroaching desert beasts, the site offers rare clues to the continent's prehistoric civilisations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher originally based out of Ratchet, has established a lonely camp beside the shattered stonework to examine curious relics known as Gahz'ridian scattered across the waste.

subzone:camp-e-thok.text: Camp E'thok. Camp E'thok is a Galak centaur settlement located in northwestern Thousand Needles. The aggressive centaur tribe uses this canyon encampment as a base to stage ambushes against passing caravans traveling through the riverbed below. Tucked into the rugged northwestern reaches of Thousand Needles, Camp E'thok serves as a key settlement for the hostile Galak centaur. Like their kin across Kalimdor, the Galak are relentlessly predatory, preying upon any travelers wandering into the canyon shadows. The camp is notorious for orchestrating raids against merchant caravans, notably ambushing the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner and seizing his goods—though his prized gadget managed to slip beyond their grasp, guarded by his fierce pet panther.

subzone:camp-kosh.text: Camp Kosh. Camp Kosh is an ogre encampment in the northern Badlands, inhabited by the aggressive Dustbelcher ogres. Perched near vital travel routes, its brutes prey on passing caravans and scavenge whatever equipment travelers leave behind in the harsh desert. Situated in the northern wastes of the Badlands, Camp Kosh serves as the northernmost settlement of the Dustbelcher ogres, who also occupy neighboring camps like Boff, Cagg, and Wurg. The ogres stationed here take advantage of their proximity to the roads, raiding vulnerable supply lines journeying toward Kargath or westward into the Searing Gorge. When dwarven prospectors led by Sigrun Ironhew were forced to flee the excavation at Uldaman, the brutes of Camp Kosh swiftly raided their abandoned wagons, hauling away precious food rations and armaments into the dusty encampment.

subzone:camp-mojache.text: Camp Mojache. Camp Mojache is the primary Horde outpost in Feralas, established as a fortified tauren settlement along the waters feeding Wildwind Lake. It provides shelter, provisions, and flight connections to travelers contending with the untamed wilderness, aggressive wildlife, and ancient ruins of the deep forest. Situated in eastern Feralas along a swift-flowing stream that feeds Wildwind Lake, Camp Mojache is a tauren settlement built to secure a foothold in the wild southern forest. While the dense jungle holds perilous threats—from savage wildlife to Gordunni ogres and aggressive Woodpaw gnolls—the camp stands as an island of safety. Equipped with lodging, trade masters, and a wind rider roost, it serves as the vital logistical hub for Horde champions operating in the region. The camp's hunters and braves are renowned for their courage and thick hides, maintaining constant vigilance against raids from the surrounding wilderness. For the Horde, holding Mojache is essential for projecting influence across Feralas, checking the presence of both the Night Elves from the coast and the dark forces lurking within Dire Maul.

subzone:cape-of-stranglethorn.text: Cape of Stranglethorn. The Cape of Stranglethorn forms the sun-baked southern tip of Stranglethorn Vale, stretching south from the Gurubashi Arena down to the ocean cliffs. Anchored by the sprawling pirate port of Booty Bay, the region is a battleground contested by goblins, Bloodsail Buccaneers, ancient jungle trolls, and encroaching wildlife. South of the ancient colosseum of Gurubashi Arena, the dense jungle gives way to the coastline known as the Cape of Stranglethorn. Dotted with crumbling troll settlements like the Ruins of Jubuwal and the Ruins of Aboraz, the cape has long since slipped from imperial Gurubashi control. Today, its beaches, coves, and jungle clearings host a chaotic mix of dangerous predators, murloc encampments, and rival pirate crews warring over trade routes and buried plunder. The dominant power along the cape is the Blackwater Raiders, led by Baron Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn from the pirate city of Booty Bay. Carved directly into the cliffs of the southern bay, this neutral harbor connects the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor via steamships to Ratchet. However, goblin control remains precarious. The Bloodsail Buccaneers operate along the southern shoals and outer islands, raiding supply lines and openly scheming to overthrow Booty Bay and seize total dominion over the South Seas.

subzone:capital-gardens.text: Capital Gardens. The Capital Gardens form the western wing of the ancient elven ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a serene, manicured park for the Kaldorei nobility, it has withered into a blighted woodland stalked by corrupted ancients, ghosts, and remnants of the Shen'dralar. Ten millennia ago, Eldre'Thalas stood as one of the shining jewels of the Kaldorei empire. The Capital Gardens served as its outdoor district, lush with enchanted flora and grand marble terraces where Highborne sorcerers debated and relaxed. Following the Great Sundering, the enclave fell on desperate times. Deprived of the Well of Eternity, the resident Shen'dralar turned to dark magic to sustain their immortality, letting the gardens wither away. Today, gray, twisted boughs and corrupted treants fill the broken courtyards, while residual magical corruption prevents the forest from ever truly healing.

subzone:cauldron.text: Cauldron. The Cauldron is a massive open-pit excavation site dominating the center of the Searing Gorge. Operated by the Dark Iron clan, this fiery quarry is worked day and night by broken slaves under the watch of cruel overseers and roving elementals. Carved deep into the scorched earth of the Searing Gorge, the Cauldron was fortified following the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros by Emperor Thaurissan. Massive, smoke-belching Dark Iron excavation machinery rims the canyon walls, scraping rock and ore from the smoldering stone. Down within its burning crevices, living fire and magma elementals prowl alongside Dark Iron taskmasters, while subterranean heat rises continuously from the depths of the mountain. Deep within the pit, captured slave workers endure brutal, endless shifts under the lash of Dark Iron overseers. Broken by relentless labor, sweltering heat, and torment, many of these laborers have been driven completely mad. They no longer recognize friend from foe, lashing out violently against any outsiders who disturb their toil—even those who might otherwise offer them a chance at liberation.

subzone:caverns-of-time.text: Caverns of Time. Tucked into the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, the Caverns of Time serve as the mystical lair of Nozdormu and the bronze dragonflight. Within its winding depths, the dragons monitor and safeguard the fragile timeways of Azeroth against any mortal intrusion or temporal tampering. Carved deep beneath the desert cliffs, the Caverns of Time are a nexus where the currents of history converge. Charged by the titans at the dawn of the world, Nozdormu the Timeless One and his bronze dragonflight act as eternal sentinels over these corridors. Inside, time behaves erratically; glimpses of past and future slip through hidden rifts, and relics plucked from distant eras lie scattered across the sands. While the great wyrm Anachronos keeps watch near the entrance, lesser bronze drakes patrol the winding descent, fiercely protective of the one true timeline. Beyond being a junction of past and future, the caverns serve as an eccentric vault. Over millennia, the bronze flight has gathered historical fragments from every corner of Azeroth: ancient dwarven structures, a watchtower from Lordaeron, chieftain quarters from the orcish clans, and armor dating back to the first kings of Stromgarde. Yet despite the occasional traveler daring to slip past the sentinels to glimpse these wonders, the inner gateways remain tightly shut, awaiting the day the flight deems mortal intervention necessary.

subzone:chamber-of-atonement.text: Chamber of Atonement. The Chamber of Atonement is the grim entrance hall to the Graveyard wing within the Scarlet Monastery. Here, beneath stone arches hung with iron chains, the Scarlet Crusade subjects captured undead and other perceived heretics to brutal interrogation and torture before casting their remains into the cloister beyond. Serving as the threshold to the Forlorn Cloister, the Chamber of Atonement is far from a sanctuary of peaceful prayer. Instead, the Scarlet Crusade has converted the grand entryway into a house of pain, outfitted with racks, shackles, and burning braziers. Zealous inquisitors use these instruments to extract confessions and torment captives, viewing excruciating pain as the only fitting penance for unholy beings. The chamber echoes constantly with the cries of the damned, presided over by cruel taskmasters who ensure that those who enter rarely walk out whole. The chamber is overseen by Interrogator Vishas, one of the Crusade's most sadistic practitioners of coercion. Vishas takes grotesque pride in breaking the resolve of anyone caught crossing the monastery's boundaries. Among his prized victims is the Forsaken captive Vorrel Sengutz, who has endured endless weeks of torment at Vishas's hands. The cruelty practiced within these walls proves to outsiders that the Scarlet Crusade's crusade for purity has twisted into wanton sadism.

subzone:chillwind-point.text: Chillwind Point. Chillwind Point is a rocky rise and ancient troll ruin sitting on the high frontier between the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the Western Plaguelands. It gets its name from the freezing drafts howling through the mountain pass out of the blighted north. Today, it serves as a lonely vantage point inhabited primarily by a lone troll mystic. Perched on the borderlands where Hillsbrad gives way to Alterac and the plagued north, Chillwind Point looks out over the mountain ravine leading directly into the Western Plaguelands. Long before Lordaeron claimed these passes, ancient trolls built stone structures upon these heights, the remnants of which still stand weather-beaten against the elements. Today, cold winds blow south through the ravine, carrying the chill of the fallen north into the foothill valleys below. Despite its bleak exposure and proximity to Scourge-ravaged lands, Chillwind Point is not entirely deserted. The ancient masonry provides shelter for Bath'rah the Windwatcher, a jungle troll hermit who communes with the violent gales coursing through the gap. Travelers and shamans venturing north often seek out his solitary camp amid the ruins to learn the secrets of the mountain currents.

subzone:circle-of-aquementas.text: Circle of Aquementas. The Circle of Aquementas is a mysterious ring of upright standing stones positioned along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, just south of Lost Rigger Cove. It serves as a ritual site where travelers can call forth the elemental spirit Aquementas. Tucked away along the windswept eastern coast of Tanaris, the Circle of Aquementas sits quietly south of the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove. Composed of weathered, upright stones arranged in a circular formation, this unusual site hums with elemental energy against the desert shore. It acts as a focus for summoning Aquementas, an elemental entity tied to an ancient artifact. While the surrounding beaches crawl with Southsea brigands and roaming sea creatures, the circle itself remains a solemn pocket of ritual power amidst the dunes.

subzone:circle-of-east-binding.text: Circle of East Binding. The Circle of East Binding is a mysterious ancient ritual site situated in the eastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands, just southwest of Hammerfall. Anchored by the Stone of East Binding, the site is violently contested and guarded by roaming water elementals known as cresting exiles. Positioned amidst the rugged highlands east of Stromgarde, the Circle of East Binding is one of several ancient sites of power scattered across the Arathi basin. At its focal point stands the Stone of East Binding, an enigmatic monument radiating potent elemental magic. Swirling water elementals known as cresting exiles roam the surrounding earth and fiercely defend the stone against any mortals who dare approach. The stones throughout Arathi are not mere natural anomalies; they function as ancient binding wards intended to suppress and imprison volatile elemental forces. The restless water spirits surrounding the eastern circle betray the strain on these wards, as the entities drawn to or trapped by the stone's magic lash out at travelers and adventurers navigating the nearby road to Hammerfall.

subzone:circle-of-inner-binding.text: Circle of Inner Binding. The Circle of Inner Binding is an ancient ring of ritual stones situated in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just east of Stromgarde Keep. Guarded by hostile earth elementals, it holds the Stone of Inner Binding, the most potent seal used to restrain the imprisoned elemental princess Myzrael deep beneath the earth. Perched upon a plateau south of the main road, the Circle of Inner Binding anchors the strongest of the ancient wards sealing Myzrael beneath Arathi. Towering slabs surround the central Stone of Inner Binding, which thrums with dense geo-magical power. Enormous rumbling earth elementals patrol the stones relentlessly, drawn to the site's resonance or bound as guardians. Despite these potent wards, cracks in this inner seal permit the trapped entity beneath the Highlands to reach out telepathically, whispering pleas for freedom to unsuspecting wanderers who handle shards of its stone.

subzone:circle-of-west-binding.text: Circle of West Binding. The Circle of West Binding is one of several ancient ritual sites scattered across the Arathi Highlands, situated near Thoradin's Wall. Centered around the Stone of West Binding, this arcane ring is overrun by fiery elemental entities bound to the site. Tucked against the rugged slopes near Thoradin's Wall, the Circle of West Binding forms part of a wider network of ritual sites dispersed throughout the Arathi Highlands. At its heart sits the Stone of West Binding, an ancient relic tied to elemental containment. The grounds are swarming with Burning Exiles—volatile fire elementals that relentlessly guard the perimeter, making any approach to the stone a perilous endeavor for travelers traversing the western plains.

subzone:clockwerk-run.text: Clockwerk Run. The Clockwerk Run is the main entrance corridor leading into the heart of fallen Gnomeregan. Stretching between the Train Depot and the Hall of Gears, this damaged hallway is heavily contaminated by toxic fallout and overrun with irradiated troggs. Serving as the primary gateway into Gnomeregan from the outer train depot, the Clockwerk Run was once a bustling conduit of gnomish logistics and transit. When High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the venting of radioactive waste to stem the trogg invasion, the corridor became a lethal trap. The blast and subsequent fighting caused portions of the hallway to collapse onto itself. Today, the passage is choked with toxic fumes and prowling irradiated troggs, making it the perilous frontline that any expedition must fight through to reach the upper Hall of Gears.

subzone:corrahn-s-dagger.text: Corrahn's Dagger. Corrahn's Dagger is the second ridge among the four mountainous fingers towering over northern Hillsbrad Foothills. This high ground serves as a hideout for rogue Syndicate operatives. Rising steeply in northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Corrahn's Dagger is the second of the four rocky projections known locally as the fingers of Hillsbrad. The ridge is overrun by cutthroats belonging to the Syndicate, who use the elevated perch to overlook the valley below.

subzone:crusader-s-armory.text: Crusader's Armory. The Crusader's Armory is a fortified interior hall within the Scarlet Monastery Armory wing. Stockpiled with munitions, gunpowder, and cannonballs, it serves as a staging ground for the zealots guarding the path toward the inner sanctum. Beyond its locked iron door lies the Hall of Champions. Situated between the Footman's Armory and the grand Hall of Champions, the Crusader's Armory displays the full military readiness of the Scarlet Crusade. Unlike the training yards outside, these narrow stone corridors are packed to the ceiling with crates of volatile gunpowder, stacked cannonballs, and heavily armed crusaders ready to repel intruders. The Crusade has turned a former monastic compound into a bristling fortress, dedicating every available hall to the tools of total war. At the far end of the armory stands a heavy locked iron door, barring entry to the inner chambers unless one holds the Scarlet Key.

subzone:crypt-badlands.text: Crypt (Badlands). Tucked away high in the dusty hills of the Badlands lies a secluded underground tomb known simply as the Crypt. Inside rests the silent remnant of an ancient warrior: an armored skeleton seated upon a stone throne, flanked by urns, chests, and a massive relic sword. Perched southeast of Hammertoe's Digsite along an unmarked earthen path rising up the hillside, the Badlands Crypt is easily missed by passersby. Down in its dark stone chambers sits an armored skeleton poised atop a throne. Resting beside the remains is the Sword of the Barbarian King, surrounded by scattered bones, urns, and forgotten chests. While miners and adventurers frequent the surrounding gullies in search of dwarven ruins and riches, the true origin and history of this seated sovereign remain a mystery lost to the arid wastes.

subzone:crypt-stromgarde-keep.text: Crypt (Stromgarde Keep). Deep within the ruins of Stromgarde Keep lies the royal crypt, situated past the sanctum chapel in the heart of the district held by the surviving Stromgarde defenders. It holds the tomb of the fallen King Thoras Trollbane and the ancestral treasures of his dynasty. Guarded closely by Prince Galen and faithful caretakers, the vault remains a sanctuary of royal honor amid a shattered kingdom. Hidden beneath the Sanctum of Stromgarde Keep, this subterranean burial vault serves as the final resting place of King Thoras Trollbane, the warrior monarch who led Stromgarde through the Second War. Despite the devastation engulfing the city—split among Syndicate rogues and Boulderfist ogres—the remaining Stromgarde militia fiercely maintains their grip on this quarter. Prince Galen Trollbane personally watches over the crypts alongside dedicated royal caretakers, ensuring his father's body and legacy remain undisturbed by the scavengers and enemies outside. Beyond housing the royal dead, the crypt safeguards prized artifacts belonging to the Trollbane lineage. Chief among these relics is Trol'kalar, the ancient runed greatsword forged centuries ago to slay trolls. Entrusted to the sworn protection of caretakers such as Alaric, Nevlin, and Weston, the chamber and its treasures are secured with powerful safeguards. Galen and his loyalists guard the tomb relentlessly, well aware that rival factions and hostile trolls across Arathi would covet the blade's ancient power.

subzone:crystal-shore.text: Crystal Shore. Crystal Shore is a stretch of sandy coastline along the southeastern edge of Stranglethorn Vale, washed by the waves of the South Seas. Tucked beneath steep coastal bluffs, the beach lies just south of the ancient Ruins of Aboraz and across the waters from Jaguero Isle. Running along the southeastern perimeter of Stranglethorn Vale, the Crystal Shore forms a natural boundary between the dense tropical interior and the open waters of the South Seas. The beach itself is walled off from the inland jungles by steep ridges, leaving only a couple of rugged passes for travelers attempting to move between the coast and the deeper wilderness of Mistvale Valley. To the north lie the crumbling troll structures of the Ruins of Aboraz, while the Wild Shore extends along the southern curves of the cape. Its location makes it a quiet, windswept margin far removed from the bustling docks of Booty Bay.

subzone:crystalvein-mine.text: Crystalvein Mine. Crystalvein Mine is a cavern in central Stranglethorn Vale, situated near the ancient ruins of Zul'Mamwe. The cavern is rich in valuable 'Singing Crystals', but aggressive native basilisks have completely overrun the site, turning prospective miners to solid stone. Tucked away in the jungle hills near Zul'Mamwe, Crystalvein Mine boasts rare deposits of Singing Crystals, a unique mineral that fetches a high price in southern trade ports. Enticed by the promise of immense profit, the Venture Company set its sights on extracting the veins. However, the mine's natural inhabitants have proved catastrophic for business. Local basilisks consume the strange crystals, hardening their scales and making them unnaturally lethal. Outside the cave mouth, petrified statues of trolls and humans stand as a silent testament to the Venture Company's failed expeditions.

subzone:dabyrie-s-farmstead.text: Dabyrie's Farmstead. Dabyrie's Farmstead is an Alliance-aligned rural settlement situated in northern Arathi Highlands. In a realm shattered by the Third War and overrun by Syndicate outlaws and Witherbark trolls, this estate remains a stubborn bastion of Stromgarde citizens led by Kenata Dabyrie. Perched in the northern fields of the Arathi Highlands, Dabyrie's Farmstead is one of the very few functioning human homesteads remaining in the fractured kingdom of Stromgarde. Owned by Kenata Dabyrie and worked alongside her sons, Fardel and Marcel, the grounds are fiercely defended by a local family militia. Surrounded by aggressive wildlife, opportunistic bandits, and the nearby Forsaken presence in the north, the farm stands as a symbol of human endurance in a ruined land.

subzone:dalaran.text: Dalaran. Dalaran was once the shining magocratic capital of the Kirin Tor, nestled on the southern shore of Lordamere Lake. Shattered by the Scourge and the demon lord Archimonde during the Third War, its surviving magi are rebuilding the city, having removed its protective violet shield early in the reconstruction. Founded after the ancient Troll Wars by sorcerers of the Arathorian Empire, Dalaran stood for centuries as humanity's premier sanctuary for arcane study. Under the leadership of the Council of Six, the Kirin Tor amassed vast magical archives and guarded powerful artifacts within the Violet Citadel. That age of splendor ended abruptly during the Third War. The traitor prince Arthas led the Scourge through the city gates to seize the Book of Medivh, and soon after, the demon lord Archimonde crushed Dalaran's soaring spires into rubble. In the aftermath of the Legion's defeat, the surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor returned to their devastated homeland. Refusing to surrender their ancestral ground to the Scourge or scavengers, they erected an impassable, shimmering violet barrier over the city's heart. The shield has since been removed, though reconstruction continues. The magi continue rebuilding their fallen sanctuary, and Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver can be found in the Violet Citadel.

subzone:dandred-s-fold.text: Dandred's Fold. Dandred's Fold is a secluded farmstead and manor tucked along the misty northwestern shores of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains. Now overrun by the Syndicate, it serves as a secure hideout for Lord Aliden Perenolde and his co-conspirators. Both the Horde and the Alliance keep a watchful eye on this lakefront retreat for very different reasons. Perched on the western edge of the Uplands with private access to the waters of Lordamere Lake, Dandred's Fold was once a tranquil country estate, likely owned by an Alteraci noble named Dandred. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the estate transformed into a fortified enclave for the Syndicate. Syndicate assassins and enforcers now patrol its fences and docks, shielding the fallen nobility from the eyes of Southshore authorities and the Forsaken across the lake.

subzone:dark-portal.text: Dark Portal. The Dark Portal is a monumental stone gateway standing at the southern rim of the Blasted Lands. First torn open through the combined sorcery of Medivh and Gul'dan, it served as the fateful conduit that brought the Old Horde into Azeroth, initiating the First War. Before its opening, this region was part of the Black Morass, a sodden wetland that stretched across the south. That changed when Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, joined his Tirisfal magics with the fel sorcery of Gul'dan on Draenor. The ritual drained untold lives and tore the fabric of reality apart. The Old Horde raised massive stone architecture to anchor the rift, marching armies through its threshold to shatter the Kingdom of Stormwind in the First War. The portal's fel emanations fundamentally corrupted the surrounding terrain, reducing lush marshes to the red, petrified wastes seen today. Following the Alliance of Lordaeron's victory in the Second War, Archmage Khadgar shattered the physical stone frame with powerful magics, hoping to sever Draenor forever. However, the dimensional tear beneath proved functionally indestructible. The Alliance erected Nethergarde Keep nearby to watch the scar, while demons and remnants of the Shadow Council continue to slink through the blasted caldera. Today the gateway stands reassembled yet dormant, a silent scar between worlds that neither side dares abandon.

subzone:darkmist-cavern.text: Darkmist Cavern. Darkmist Cavern is an abandoned mine tucked into northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, completely infested with predatory giant spiders. Crumbling ruins outside hint at an unfortunate former settlement swallowed up by the marsh's hazards. Locals remain divided on whether the cavern gave its name to the arachnids or the reverse. Situated in the northwest reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Darkmist Cavern appears to have once been an active mining venture. Today, any human presence has long vanished, leaving behind rotting, ruined shacks outside the entrance and a network of tunnels choked with thick webs. The cavern is overrun by Darkmist spiders, predatory horrors whose venom and size make the tunnels deadly to unwary wanderers. Marsh dwellers still dispute whether the cavern was named after the foul brood nesting inside or if the spiders took the title from the misty cave itself. Despite the obvious danger, the cavern attracts occasional scavengers and eccentric marshfolk. The hermit 'Swamp Eye' Jarl is notorious for sending travelers deep into the webs to harvest the eyes of these monstrous spiders, insisting they make a fine stock for broth. Aside from such eccentric culinary outings, most sensible travelers steer well clear of the web-strewn entrance.

subzone:darrow-hill.text: Darrow Hill. Darrow Hill is an elevated expanse of rugged grassland nestled in northern Hillsbrad Foothills directly beneath the Headland. While mountain lions and stags graze across its open slopes, feral yetis lurk inside the Foothill Caverns that pit the hillside. Rich with veins of Alterac Granite, it serves as a treacherous frontier where natural beasts and rival travelers constantly clash. Rising along the base of the northern mountains below the Headland, Darrow Hill bridges the rolling pasture of southern Hillsbrad with the jagged, colder heights of Alterac. Mountain lions and stags stalk through the tall grasses, sharing the rocky slopes with towering yetis that spill out from the Foothill Caverns. Beyond its feral wildlife, the cavern walls hide deposits of dense Alterac Granite, drawing quarry workers, miners, and adventurers straight into harm's way. Caught between contentious regional claims, its trails remain notoriously dangerous for travelers of either faction caught unawares.

subzone:deadwood-village.text: Deadwood Village. Deadwood Village is a furbolg encampment nestled in southern Felwood. Once a peaceful clan attuned to nature, its residents fell victim to the demonic corruption that blighted the surrounding forest. Driven mad by fel taint, the Deadwood furbolgs now attack anyone who approaches their crude wooden settlement. Situated near the southern border of Felwood, Deadwood Village serves as the primary enclave of the Deadwood tribe. When the Burning Legion's demonic energies washed through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs lacked the power to resist the creeping rot. Their minds warped by fel malice, they abandoned their ancient traditions and spiritual harmony. Today, the village is a squalid gathering of hostile brutes, shamans, and den watchers who violently defend their polluted grounds against intruders, earning the despair of their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

subzone:dire-maul.text: Dire Maul. Dire Maul is the ruined expanse of Eldre'Thalas, an ancient Highborne city hidden deep in the wilderness of Feralas. Once built to safeguard Queen Azshara's arcane secrets, its crumbling plazas and towering coliseums are now divided between occupying Gordok ogres, invading satyrs, and the withered remnants of its original elven caretakers. Twelve thousand years ago, Eldre'Thalas served as a wondrous bastion for Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin wove a magical barrier that shielded the city from ruin. Severed from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped a colossal demon named Immol'thar beneath their sanctum, siphoning its fel essence to sustain their immortality and arcane powers for millennia.

subzone:direforge-hill.text: Direforge Hill. Direforge Hill is a rugged highland in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. The Dark Iron dwarf warlock Balgaras the Foul commands a hostile encampment on its slopes. Direforge Hill serves as a major Dark Iron campsite in the northeastern Wetlands. Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron dwarf warlock, commands the hostile dwarves occupying the hill southeast of Dun Modr. The Dark Iron dwarves occupying Direforge Hill pose a threat to travelers through the northeastern Wetlands. Balgaras the Foul commands the hostile encampment.

subzone:dragonmaw-gates.text: Dragonmaw Gates. The Dragonmaw Gates are a series of imposing fortifications along the mountain road leading up from the eastern Wetlands. Built to guard the steep ascent to the mountain fortress of Grim Batol, these heavy barricades bar entry into the cursed heights of the dwarven ruins. Carved into the rugged peaks bordering the eastern Wetlands, the Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road that climbs into the mountains toward Grim Batol. Named after the Dragonmaw clan of orcs who held the dwarven mountain city during the Second War, these defensive barriers remain deeply fortified checkpoints. Anyone attempting to ascend toward the heights must contend with the lingering perils of the pass, where powerful drakes and grim reminders of the clan's dark history still cast a long shadow. Though the Dragonmaw orcs were broken and scattered following the destruction of the Demon Soul, the mountain path remains exceptionally dangerous. Powerful red dragons have been seen watching over the winding slopes and perches around the gates. Between monstrous drakes and remnants of the Dragonmaw clan lurking in the nearby hills, the gates stand as a firm barrier against any travelers bold enough to venture up the heights.

subzone:dragonmurk.text: Dragonmurk. Dragonmurk is a sprawling, hazardous tract of southern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with black dragonspawn and hatchlings. Flanked by ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns, it serves as the hostile outer perimeter for the brood of Onyxia. Spanning the southern interior of Dustwallow Marsh, the Dragonmurk marks the threshold where damp wetlands give way to the dominion of the black dragonflight. The waterways and thick mud here crawl with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and ravenous whelps. The surrounding landscape has suffered deeply from their presence; adjacent territories such as the ruined village of Stonemaul and the scorched cavern known as the Den of Flame have both fallen completely under the flight's territorial grip.

subzone:dreadmaul-post.text: Dreadmaul Post. Dreadmaul Post is an entrenched ogre settlement situated in the scorched wastes of the Blasted Lands. Established by the Dreadmaul clan, this mound serves as a fortified redoubt near the Dark Portal where ogres have lingered since their arrival from Draenor. Travelers passing through the region must contend with these fierce brutes and the treacherous terrain surrounding their encampment. When the Horde surged through the Dark Portal in decades past, clans of ogres marched alongside them into Azeroth. The Dreadmaul clan chose to dig in near the gateway itself, raising crude stone mounds and earthworks across the red wastes of the Blasted Lands. Dreadmaul Post stands as one of their primary outposts, maintaining a firm grip over the badlands and clashing with wandering beasts and any travelers foolish enough to draw near their territory.

subzone:dreadmurk-shore.text: Dreadmurk Shore. Dreadmurk Shore encompasses the foggy coastline and scattered islands of Dustwallow Marsh running north toward the Barrens. Dominated by aggressive Mirefin murlocs and sea beasts, these treacherous waters have recently become the hiding ground for shipwrecked Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold, Dreadmurk Shore is a dismal expanse of muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands. The coast is overrun by the Mirefin tribe, a territorial clan of murlocs that aggressively attacks any travelers nearing their coastal villages. Sea turtles and aquatic predators prowl the shallows, making the shoreline dangerous to navigate even without factoring in the surrounding swamplands.

subzone:drowned-reef.text: Drowned Reef. The Drowned Reef is a treacherous stretch of coastal waters off the southern cliffs of the Arathi Highlands. Beneath the waves lie ancient sunken ruins, claimed by hostile Daggerspine naga who appear able to control the bay's tides, endangering passing vessels. Just outside the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, the Drowned Reef forms a watery graveyard for navigators. Shattered ships, including the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine, lie submerged beneath the waves. Daggerspine naga led by Prince Nazjak inhabit the reef and appear able to control the bay's tides, dooming crews seeking refuge in the cove. Those brave or foolish enough to dive into the deep water will discover the submerged architecture of an ancient elven city. Calcified elven gems remain among its drowned ruins.

subzone:drowned-sacellum.text: Drowned Sacellum. The Drowned Sacellum is a submerged elven shrine lying just inside the entrance of Blackfathom Deeps. Submerged beneath brackish saltwater and draped in cavernous roots, its shattered masonry is now overrun by murlocs and makrura. Stepping through the threshold of Blackfathom Deeps immediately brings explorers into the Drowned Sacellum. Once a tranquil subterranean chapel dedicated to Elune, the sacellum has long collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Saltwater pools swallow ancient marble flagstones overgrown with starfish, while massive tree roots dangle from the cavern ceiling above. Dark, flickering wisps provide the only dim light in the gloom, illuminating a ruined pathway of stones that adventurers must carefully navigate to reach the Pool of Ask'ar deeper within the temple complex. Long abandoned by its night elf caretakers, the Drowned Sacellum has fallen into the hands of shoreline scavengers. Packs of aggressive murlocs and heavily armored makrura dwell side by side in the murky waters, attacking anyone who dares disturb their nesting grounds. While darker, cultic threats lurk further below in the temple depths, these predatory creatures form the first hazardous line of defense for the subterranean ruins.

subzone:drywhisker-gorge.text: Drywhisker Gorge. Drywhisker Gorge is a rugged cleft in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, situated northeast of the Horde outpost of Hammerfall. The gorge and its inner cavern are held by a hostile clan of kobolds, who fiercely guard rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried deep underground. Tucked away in the mountainous folds east of Hammerfall, Drywhisker Gorge serves as the primary redoubt of the Drywhisker clan of kobolds. While kobolds are often dismissed as simple mine pests, the Drywhiskers in Arathi are heavily entrenched. They guard their subterranean passages with fierce territorial tenacity, working veins of rare Lesser Bloodstone Ore and defending the deep recesses of the earth. Their proximity makes them a persistent nuisance to the nearby orcs of Hammerfall.

subzone:dunemaul-compound.text: Dunemaul Compound. Dunemaul Compound serves as the central settlement and ogre mound for the Dunemaul clan in Tanaris. Tucked into the rocky ridges bordering the desert wastes, it houses the clan's brute enforcers and spellcasters. Carved into the rugged desert rock of western Tanaris, the Dunemaul Compound is the primary stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres. These hulking desert dwellers have adapted to the harsh arid climate, scratching out an existence through brute force and opportunism. The compound itself centers on an ogre mound and cave network. Though primitive, the clan fields a dangerous mix of warriors, enforcers, and twisted spellcasters practicing dark warlock and mage magics. For travelers journeying across the dunes, the settlement is a treacherous den of aggressive giants who violently reject uninvited guests.

subzone:dustbowl.text: Dustbowl. The Dustbowl is a sprawling, arid expanse in the northwestern Badlands, lying between the Horde outpost of Kargath and the central Valley of Fangs. Swept by scouring desert winds, it is a harsh wilderness populated by scavengers, prowling beasts, and wandering elementals. It is also the site of Camp Wurg, making it a frequent crossing point for travelers braving the wasteland. Stretching across the northwest of the Badlands, the Dustbowl is characterized by dry gulches, cracked clay, and relentless winds that stir up choking plumes of grit. Despite the barren landscape, tough desert flora persists in the form of hardy cacti and scattered, gnarled trees. The open flatland presents constant danger to unguided wayfarers, who must contend with predatory coyotes, circling buzzards, and living rock elementals born of the rugged earth. Tucked within this scrubland lies Camp Wurg, providing a recognizable landmark amidst the otherwise desolate expanse.

subzone:dustfire-valley.text: Dustfire Valley. Dustfire Valley is a dry, windswept gulch nestled along the northern edge of the Searing Gorge. It serves as the scorched threshold leading directly to the fortified gate of Stonewrought Pass, which bars the mountain route into Loch Modan. Tucked away in northern Searing Gorge, Dustfire Valley is defined by choking ash, brittle rock, and barren canyon walls. Its most notable feature is the imposing, locked dwarven gateway sealing Stonewrought Pass. Because of these locked iron doors, direct travel north into the Valley of Kings and Loch Modan remains entirely barred to ordinary wanderers, leaving the valley an isolated cul-de-sac amidst the sulfurous wastes.

subzone:dustwallow-bay.text: Dustwallow Bay. Dustwallow Bay is an inlet of the Great Sea tucked between the sodden coast of Dustwallow Marsh and the fortified port of Theramore Isle. Its brackish coastal shallows teem with marine life, treacherous shoals, and secluded coves just off the main maritime routes of eastern Kalimdor. Dustwallow Bay defines the coastal boundary where the stagnant, murky wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh meet the open waters of the Great Sea. Flanked to the east by Theramore Isle, the bay serves as an oceanic approach for vessels arriving at Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island haven. Despite heavy maritime traffic running to and from the docks, the surrounding coastline remains wild and hazardous, pocked with rocky outcrops, murloc encampments, and tucked-away inlets like Tidefury Cove. While the marsh itself is infested with crocolisks and hostile beasts, the bay's islands and inlets draw those who seek isolation and rich catches. The small islets dotting the waters near Tidefury Cove provide a secluded retreat for anglers, most notably the legendary fisherman Nat Pagle, who can often be found angling off the rocks away from the bustling city of Theramore.

subzone:eastern-strand.text: Eastern Strand. The Eastern Strand is a stretch of southern coastline in Hillsbrad Foothills, lying to the southeast toward the border of the Arathi Highlands. Once peaceful shores, the beaches and shallows have been overrun by hostile Daggerspine naga establishing a coastal beachhead. Running along the southeastern edge of Hillsbrad Foothills, the Eastern Strand complements the Western Strand across the bay. While the region is primarily known for human farming settlements and territorial clashes between Southshore and Tarren Mill, these sandy flats and tidelines are dominated entirely by the Daggerspine naga. Creeping out of the Great Sea, the serpent folk slither across the sandbars and dwell among the rocky outcrops, watching the mainland closely.

subzone:eastmoon-ruins.text: Eastmoon Ruins. The Eastmoon Ruins are an ancient troll archaeological site situated in eastern Tanaris, perched just west of the Gaping Chasm. Once built by the desert empires of old, the crumbling stone masonry is now occupied by Dunemaul ogres using the remnants as a desert encampment. Rising out of the blistering desert floor just west of the insect-infested Gaping Chasm, the Eastmoon Ruins preserve the crumbling architecture of ancient troll civilization. Decaying pillars, weathered stone plazas, and sun-bleached monuments hint at a time long before the sands swallowed this region. Rather than scholars or troll descendants tending the shrines, the site is firmly held by the Dunemaul ogres, who rely on the broken walls for shelter and vantage over nearby trade routes.

subzone:eldreth-row.text: Eldreth Row. Eldreth Row comprises the soaring, ruined outer halls forming the western entrance to Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a grand threshold of ancient Eldre'Thalas, the area is now choked with overgrowth and fiercely patrolled by Gordunni ogres. Standing as the outermost perimeter of ancient Eldre'Thalas, Eldreth Row is an imposing avenue of high-arched elven architecture that sits just outside the deeper quarters and the Broken Commons. Centuries of neglect have cracked its stonework, allowing the creeping flora of Feralas to reclaim its colonnades. Today, the pristine majesty of the Highborne has been replaced by the crude dominance of the Gordunni ogres, who use the halls as an outer staging ground, guarding the paths leading east toward the Warpwood Quarter and west past the Dire Pool.

subzone:emerald-sanctuary.text: Emerald Sanctuary. The Emerald Sanctuary is an outpost of the Cenarion Circle situated at the southern entrance of Felwood. Here, night elven and tauren druids unite to study the pervasive demonic taint and attempt the arduous task of healing the corrupted woodland. Perched on the southern edge of Felwood near the Ashenvale border, the Emerald Sanctuary serves as the primary base of operations for the Cenarion Circle in this blighted wilderness. Unlike the bitter factional conflicts burning across Kalimdor, this sanctuary offers a neutral foothold where druids look past politics to focus entirely on ecological restoration. From here, researchers track corrupted flora and direct investigations toward Jaedenar, seeking any viable method to cleanse the poisoned soil.

subzone:ethel-rethor.text: Ethel Rethor. Ethel Rethor is an ancient night elven ruin situated along the rugged northwestern coast of Desolace. While a solitary, sealed tower still rises above the waves, the majority of the sunken settlement now lies submerged in the sea and overrun by hostile naga. Perched on the desolate coast of western Kalimdor, Ethel Rethor stands as a haunting reminder of the ancient night elven civilization that flourished before the Great Sundering. Much of the grand architecture has collapsed into the ocean depths, leaving only shattered foundations and a lone, weathered tower protruding from the surf. A small bridge extends toward the tower's sealed portal, but the structure remains shut tight against the elements and intruders alike. The submerged chambers and surrounding shallows have become a stronghold for coastal naga, making the waters treacherous for any who wander near. Despite its remote location and serpentine infestation, Ethel Rethor draws travelers interested in Kalimdor's forgotten histories and ongoing threats. An agent of the Argent Dawn, Azore Aldamort, maintains a watchful presence near the ruins, monitoring the naga menace and offering aid to intrepid adventurers willing to dive into the sunken passages. Between the aquatic dangers offshore and the barren wastes inland, the ruins serve as a lonely coastal crossroads.

subzone:faldir-s-cove.text: Faldir's Cove. Faldir's Cove is a secluded natural harbor nestled along the southern coastline of the Arathi Highlands. Steeped in human history, it is traditionally remembered as the departure point from which early settlers sailed south to found Stormwind. Today, it serves as an emergency shelter for stranded Blackwater Raiders whose fleet ran afoul of local hazards. Tucked away behind the rugged bluffs south of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove is linked to the mainland by a concealed cave tunnel. The cove honors the memory of Faldir, the ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition set sail from these very shores to cross the Great Sea and establish the southern kingdom of Stormwind. In the present day, however, its quiet waters house a very different crowd: an expedition of Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay, led by Captains Steelgut and O'Breen, who sailed north pursuing ancient elven treasures only to end up trapped in the bay. The Blackwater venture turned catastrophic upon reaching the Arathi coast. Strange and unnatural tides conjured by the territorial naga dwelling on the offshore Drowned Reef shattered two of their three vessels. Only the Harbinger survived intact, limping into Faldir's Cove. With the naga prowling the waters and their navigation charts resting beneath the waves, the surviving pirates and their gnomish researchers find themselves marooned, reliant on neutral travelers to battle the aquatic horrors and recover sunken salvage.

subzone:fallow-sanctuary.text: Fallow Sanctuary. The Fallow Sanctuary is a secluded village hidden deep within the bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as home to an isolated tribe of mutated draenei known as the Lost Ones, whose severe grief and homesickness have driven them feral. Tucked away among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallow Sanctuary was established by stranded Lost Ones seeking a place of their own. Severed from their ancestral world and deformed by dark energies, these wretched outcasts found no peace in the marshland. Over time, relentless sorrow and isolation shattered their sanity, reducing the tribe to a hostile, feral state where they fiercely attack any outsiders who trespass into their village. The settlement was once guided by figures like Ongeku and Noboru the Cudgel, though the village's leadership crumbled following their absence and demise.

subzone:feathermoon-stronghold-classic.text: Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). Feathermoon Stronghold is a fortified night elf bastion situated on Sardor Isle off the western shores of Feralas. Established by General Shandris Feathermoon, it serves as the Alliance's primary staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Perched on Sardor Isle just off the Forgotten Coast, Feathermoon Stronghold stands as a crucial bulwark for the Night Elves and the broader Alliance. Built under the direction of General Shandris Feathermoon—Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted lieutenant for ten millennia—the fortress projects Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Its isolated island geography shields it from the beasts, ogres, and Horde interlopers prowling the primeval jungles of mainland Feralas. Given its insular position, Feathermoon relies heavily on sea and air links to maintain logistics. A small passenger boat regularly shuttles travellers across the channel between Sardor Isle and the Forgotten Coast dock. For distant travel, a dedicated hippogryph roost ties the stronghold directly to major Alliance hubs, including Thalanaar on the Thousand Needles border, Nijel's Point in the Desolace highlands, and Auberdine in the north.

subzone:felpaw-village.text: Felpaw Village. Felpaw Village is a corrupted furbolg settlement nestled in the far northern reaches of Felwood, guarding the mountain path leading directly to Timbermaw Hold. Inhabited by the fallen Deadwood tribe, its huts and gathering grounds are tainted by demonic influence and hostile to all outsiders. Situated at the northern edge of Felwood, Felpaw Village serves as the primary northern redoubt for the fallen Deadwood furbolgs. Once gentle forest wardens, the tribe fell victim to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War, driving them into a state of feral madness. Now, the village stands as a blighted enclave filled with crude huts, ritual totems, and hostile warriors who attack anyone wandering near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold. The proximity of Felpaw Village to the sacred entrance of Timbermaw Hold makes it a critical threat to the few uncorrupted furbolgs remaining in the region. The Timbermaw guards posted at the northern mouth of Felwood view their fallen cousins with a mixture of mourning and vigilance, frequently calling upon travelers to cull the Deadwood ranks, seize their ritual fetishes, and keep the corruption from spilling through the gates into Moonglade and Winterspring.

subzone:feral-scar-vale.text: Feral Scar Vale. Feral Scar Vale is a rocky gorge tucked within the High Wilderness of western Feralas. Overrun by territorial Feral Scar yetis, its cavernous tunnels are notoriously perilous to travelers who venture off the overgrown forest trails. Situated amid the thick foliage and sheer cliffs of the High Wilderness, Feral Scar Vale serves as the primary den for the savage Feral Scar yetis. While yetis are common in the snowy peaks of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these primal brutes have adapted completely to the wild, humid climate of Feralas. They fiercely defend the vale's cave network, hoarding bone trophies and aggressively driving off any intruders who wander into their hunting grounds. Beyond the primal danger of the yetis, the deeper recesses of Feral Scar Vale hide unexpected oddities. Gnomish engineering distress signals have occasionally been tracked into these dark caverns, where lost exploratory devices—such as stranded robotic survey chickens—have ended up trapped by the ferocious beasts, awaiting activation and extraction.

subzone:fire-plume-ridge.text: Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano rising directly from the center of Un'Goro Crater. Its searing slopes and subterranean magma channels fuel the crater's geysers and steam pools while playing host to fierce fire elementals. Towering over the primeval basin of Un'Goro, Fire Plume Ridge stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding lush jungle. Lava steadily cascades down its scorched rock faces, carving a landscape of ash and basalt. Subterranean magma arteries spiderweb outward beneath the soil from the ridge, fueling the bubbling geysers and hot springs scattered across the basin. The oppressive heat here is legendary—far exceeding ordinary volcanic temperatures according to goblin measuring devices—making it perilous for ill-prepared explorers to wander without ample water and shade. The volcano is an elemental furnace teeming with living flame. Living flares and roving fire elementals patrol the glowing flows, drawn to the concentration of pure subterranean heat. Deep within a cavern near the volcanic summit resides Blazerunner, the undisputed master among Un'Goro's elemental denizens. Venturing high up the ridge means navigating both lethal heat and volatile elemental spirits that aggressively defend their fiery domain.

subzone:firewatch-ridge.text: Firewatch Ridge. Firewatch Ridge is a high volcanic bluff in the northern reaches of Searing Gorge, serving as a primary encampment for the Dark Iron dwarves. Looming directly above the vast excavation known as the Cauldron, the ridge is heavily fortified by dwarven sentries, mechanical golems, and nesting fire spiders. To the northwest, an ominous cave system reveals an entrenched presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Perched above the industrial devastation of the Cauldron, Firewatch Ridge functions as a critical staging ground for the Dark Iron clan's operations in Searing Gorge. Dwarven guards, engineers, and molten golem creations patrol the crags, fiercely defending their foothold alongside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. Its elevation provides the Dark Irons an unobstructed view of the surrounding ash plains, ensuring early warning against rival incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the ridge lies an underground cave network claimed by the Twilight's Hammer. These cultists operate in the shadows of the Dark Iron encampment, conducting dark rituals and harboring powerful elite zealots beneath the rock. Their proximity to both the Dark Iron infrastructure and Blackrock Mountain reflects the pervasive, insidious reach of elemental and apocalyptic cults within the fiery heart of the Searing Gorge.

subzone:forgotten-coast.text: Forgotten Coast. The Forgotten Coast forms the wild western shore of Feralas, where the ancient rainforest meets the Veiled Sea. Lumbering sea giants and water elementals roam this battered strand. Stretching along the western edge of Feralas, the Forgotten Coast is a windswept shoreline confronting the expanse of the Veiled Sea. Unlike the dense canopy inland, this frontier is exposed to the elements and dominated by towering sea giants and roving water elementals pacing the surf. Travelers emerging from the forest canopy must contend with these primeval coastal guardians while navigating access to the sea, where ferry connections link to the night elven bastion of Sardor Isle.

subzone:forgotten-pool.text: Forgotten Pool. The Forgotten Pool is a submerged cavern tucked deep beneath the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Located beyond the Moonshrine Ruins, this quiet dead-end serves as the aquatic lair of monstrous deep-sea predators lurking in the subterranean dark. Reaching the Forgotten Pool requires diving into the sunken subterranean waterways extending past the Moonshrine Ruins. Cut off from dry ground, the pool is an isolated, stagnant cavern completely flooded by dark waters. Away from the chanting Twilight's Hammer cultists and the patrolling naga, this secluded pocket serves as the lair of the ancient aquatic terror known as Old Serra'kis, keeping the beast hidden in the flooded dark.

subzone:forlorn-ridge.text: Forlorn Ridge. Forlorn Ridge is a towering mountain ridge looming over southwestern Azshara. Its strategic elevation and commanding views over the coast have drawn the attention of both the Alliance and the Horde, who have each carved out fortifications along its slopes. Rising sharply above the autumnal forests of western Azshara, Forlorn Ridge dominates the surrounding terrain. Resembling an ancient, long-dormant volcano, its high vantage point offers a sweeping view over the coastal approaches and the ruined elven estates below. Because control over these heights dictates military dominance in the sector, both Alliance and Horde forces have established encampments and outposts along its mountain flanks, watching each other warily across the rugged bluffs.

subzone:frayfeather-highlands.text: Frayfeather Highlands. The Frayfeather Highlands form an elevated wilderness in the dense forests of Feralas. This remote plateau is the ancestral roost and nesting ground of the wild Frayfeather hippogryphs. Intrepid scavengers and naturalists often brave its territorial flocks in search of intact hippogryph eggs. Rising above the surrounding forest floor of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are dominated by steep slopes and crags where wild hippogryphs raise their broods. The local flocks are notoriously aggressive toward intruders, fiercely defending the scattered nests tucked among the rock shelves. Because these beasts are so well adapted to the rugged cliffs, their nesting grounds have drawn significant interest from outsiders—most notably goblin entrepreneurs in distant Gadgetzan who seek unhatched eggs for study and profit.

subzone:fungal-rock.text: Fungal Rock. Fungal Rock is a damp, cavernous hollow carved into the northeastern cliff walls of Un'Goro Crater. Dominated by aggressive primates and thick growths of Ghost Mushrooms, it is one of the crater's most dangerous ape dens. Tucked behind a small waterfall and pool along Un'Goro Crater's northeastern edge, Fungal Rock serves as the primary den for the region's massive gorillas. Inside the damp, subterranean corridors, towering Un'Goro Stompers and Thunderers patrol among clusters of rare Ghost Mushrooms. The deepest recesses house territorial behemoths, including the mighty silverback U'cha and the elusive albino gorilla Uhk'loc. Beyond its primal inhabitants, curious travelers may stumble upon artificial oddities near the cave mouth, such as A-Me 01, a damaged mechanical ape abandoned by gnome researchers.

subzone:gadgetzan.text: Gadgetzan. Gadgetzan is the walled desert hub of the Steamwheedle Cartel, standing as an island of commerce in northern Tanaris. Open to both Horde and Alliance travelers, the town operates under strictly enforced goblin neutrality, welcoming anyone with coin to spend or odd jobs to undertake. Surrounded by scorching sands, Gadgetzan serves as the regional heart for the Steamwheedle Cartel's ventures in southern Kalimdor. Built with characteristic goblin ingenuity and haphazard architecture, the town boasts an independent auction house, bank, inn, and specialized crafting facilities for engineers, blacksmiths, and alchemists. It also houses flight masters catering to both major factions, ensuring steady traffic of adventurers heading toward Tanaris, Feralas, and the untamed basin of Un'Goro. Above all, commerce rules supreme: as long as visitors keep their weapons sheathed and their purses open, they are safe within its gates. Peace in Gadgetzan is maintained not by good will, but by heavily armed goblin bruisers who swiftly pummel anyone who threatens trade or instigates faction brawls. Beyond the gates, however, life is precarious. The Gadgetzan Water Company constantly battles the Wastewander bandits, a ruthless gang occupying the vital Waterspring Field. Water is liquid gold in Tanaris, and the cartel frequently hires outside mercenaries to eliminate bandit leadership and reclaim vital water pouches to keep the town's reservoirs functional.

subzone:gallery-of-treasures.text: Gallery of Treasures. The Gallery of Treasures is an ornate, heavily guarded corridor inside the Scarlet Monastery's halls, connecting the Huntsman's Cloister to the Athenaeum. Lined with recovered paintings, relics, and illuminated texts, it showcases the wealth and Lordaeron heritage preserved by the Scarlet Crusade amidst their zealous war against the undead. Situated deep within the Library wing of the Scarlet Monastery, the Gallery of Treasures serves as a grand hall connecting the kennels of the Huntsman's Cloister to the sacred archives of the Athenaeum. Unlike the hound pens of the cloister, this corridor is lined with fine paintings, historical artifacts, and small chambers filled with books salvaged from across the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. To the Scarlet Crusade, these relics represent the untainted legacy of humanity they have sworn to protect, fiercely guarded against all outsiders who dare intrude upon their sanctuary.

subzone:gaping-chasm.text: Gaping Chasm. The Gaping Chasm is a sprawling silithid hive carved deep into the sands of southeastern Tanaris. Infested by aggressive insectoid horrors of the Hazzali brood, it serves as a grim warning of the growing silithid menace spreading beyond the western deserts. Breaking the rolling expanses of Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm plunges down into a teeming subterranean warren of tunnels, resinous mounds, and twitching carapaces. This hive belongs to the Hazzali, an aggressive brood of silithid that have burrowed beneath the desert wastes. Between subterranean stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers, any travelers or treasure-hunters foolish enough to descend into the chasm quickly find themselves hunted as prey or preserved in sticky cocoons. The expanding hive caught the attention of Gadgetzan's enterprising minds, prompting Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser to dispatch his junior surveyor, Scrimshank, into the pit to map and measure the geological shifts caused by the insect tunnels. Unsurprisingly, the expedition ended in disaster.
