Scrimshank met a grim end amidst the chittering broods, leaving behind scattered gear and measuring instruments that caution anyone against underestimating the silithid threat.

subzone:gelkis-village.text: Gelkis Village. Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor. Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

subzone:ghost-walker-post.text: Ghost Walker Post. Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade. Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands. Led by the tauren shaman Gurda Wildmane, the spiritual heart of the outpost is closely entwined with the neighboring Kodo Graveyard. Shamans stationed here tend to the dying beasts that wander in to perish, helping ease them into the next life and communing with their lingering spirits. Between spiritual communion and constant military readiness, the defenders of the post honor the ancient bond between the tauren and the mighty kodo amid the ashes of Desolace.

subzone:golakka-hot-springs.text: Golakka Hot Springs. Golakka Hot Springs is a geothermal basin in western Un'Goro Crater, nestled just north of Terror Run. Its bubbling pools and erupting geysers are fueled by the intense volcanic activity of nearby Fire Plume Ridge. The mineral-rich waters attract eccentric researchers, alchemists in search of exotic reagents, and wandering water elementals known as Steaming Furies. Situated in the western reaches of Un'Goro Crater, the Golakka Hot Springs are a direct product of the subterranean heat radiating from Fire Plume Ridge. Scalding water bubbles continuously to the surface, shaping tiered mineral terraces and violently erupting geysers. The environment is heavily prowled by Steaming Furies, elemental manifestations born from the convergence of subterranean groundwater and volcanic heat. Despite the danger, the springs frequently draw explorers, herbalists, and researchers fascinated by the crater's unique geology. The unique properties of Golakka's waters have drawn interest beyond simple sightseeing. Alchemists value the geothermally enriched spring water as a potent catalytic reagent, even utilizing it in delicate concotions such as love potions. The geothermal vent also hosts quirky visitors, such as Spark Nilminer perched atop the central geyser vent, and draws the researcher Krakle, who seeks to decipher how the hot springs directly tap into the volcanic heart of the crater.

subzone:gordok-commons.text: Gordok Commons. The Gordok Commons comprise the fortified northern quarter of the ancient Highborne ruins of Dire Maul. Under the rule of King Gordok, this sprawling stone complex serves as the seat of power for the elite warrior caste of the Gordunni ogres. Occupying what was once an aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas, the Gordok Commons have been thoroughly desecrated and refitted for ogre tastes. Grand night elven pillars and arched passageways now house armories, crude barricades, and training grounds for the Gordok—the fiercest, most disciplined fighters among the Gordunni clan. At the deepest end of the wing lies Gordok's Seat, where King Gordok presides over his brutes through sheer force and intimidation. Gordok culture operates entirely on brutal precedent: might makes right. According to clan tradition, whoever slays the sitting monarch claims the title of King Gordok, earning immediate obedience from any surviving captains and guards. Astute intruders exploit this custom by sneaking or scheming past the king's lieutenants rather than slaying them outright. If a challenger executes only the king, the surviving guards will recognize the victor's authority and present lavish tributes rather than fight to avenge their former ruler.

subzone:gordunni-outpost.text: Gordunni Outpost. Tucked into the rugged cliffs north of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost serves as a fortified camp for the brutish Gordunni ogres of Feralas. The clan's corrupting influence has choked the once-vibrant wilderness here, leaving the surrounding earth dry, withered, and brown. Carved into the northern mountains above the Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost stands out as a stark scar against the lush canopy of Feralas. Wherever the Gordunni ogres settle, their reckless magical channeling and destructive habits sap the vitality of the wild, leaving the local flora dead and the hillsides barren. The outpost consists of dirt trails, a shallow entrance cave, and a larger ogre mound burrowed deep into the rear cliffs. Patrolled by heavily armed hillguards, cunning channelers, and ogre tamers, the camp also holds dangerous trophies—including a captured sasquatch named Bigfist kept in crude confinement near the deeper den.

subzone:green-belt.text: Green Belt. The Green Belt is a wild stretch of marshland in the eastern Wetlands, sprawling below the ridges of Grim Batol. It is overrun by roaming bog beasts, predatory crocolisks, and toxic oozes, guarded primarily by the solitary night elf Rethiel the Greenwarden. Stretching across the eastern interior of the Wetlands, the Green Belt is one of the sodden region's untamed hollows. The local wildlife—ranging from massive crocolisks to shifting oozes and shambling bog beasts—makes travel through the mossy waters hazardous. Deep within its reaches sits a solitary watch post manned by Rethiel the Greenwarden, a lone night elf dedicated to studying the fen's ecology and keeping its hostile denizens in check. Scattered amidst the muck lies the wreckage of a Dragonmaw clan caravan, left behind after the catastrophic battle at nearby Grim Batol. Crimson whelplings still linger around the broken carts and crushed cages, haunting reminders of the orcish clan's past enslavement of Alexstrasza and her red dragon brood.

subzone:grimesilt-dig-site.text: Grimesilt Dig Site. Grimesilt Dig Site is an archaeological excavation in the Searing Gorge originally broken ground by Ironforge dwarves. Overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves, the pit is now firmly under enemy control while surviving members of the original expedition struggle to endure in hiding. Situated within the soot-choked badlands of the Searing Gorge, the Grimesilt Dig Site began as an expedition sanctioned by Ironforge scholars seeking relics beneath the crags. That venture met a violent end when the native Dark Iron dwarves drove out the excavators and claimed the equipment for themselves. Today, the trench swarms with Dark Iron sentries, leaving the wounded and scattered survivors of the original Ironforge crew trapped in and around the pit.

subzone:grom-gol-base-camp.text: Grom'gol Base Camp. Grom'gol Base Camp is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in Stranglethorn Vale, situated along the western coast of northern Stranglethorn. Commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh, the settlement secures a critical foothold and supply chain in the southern Eastern Kingdoms. With direct zeppelin towers linking to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, it stands as an armed staging ground against local jungle troll tribes and hostile Alliance forces. Carved into the dense jungle of northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, Grom'gol Base Camp is a fortified military bastion commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh. Ringed by defensive palisades and heavily armed grunts, the base camp endures non-stop harassment from Bloodscalp headhunters, lurking naga, and prowling beasts. Despite these threats, its vital strategic location secures safe supply routes north toward Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows while keeping a watchful eye on Alliance traffic descending from Duskwood or traveling up from Booty Bay. Grom'gol's prominent wooden zeppelin towers serve as one of the most vital logistical hubs in the Eastern Kingdoms. Goblin skycraft tethered here maintain regular routes directly to the capital cities of Orgrimmar and the Undercity. This uninterrupted airbridge allows Horde forces to rapidly deploy reinforcements and resources straight into the heart of Stranglethorn without braving Alliance-dominated highways or the deep sea.

subzone:growless-cave.text: Growless Cave. Growless Cave is a frigid cavern carved into the crags of the Alterac Mountains, overrun by ferocious mountain yetis. It is best known as the resting place of the Flame of Uzel, an unholy ceremonial pyre tied to the dark necromancy of Helcular. Tucked away in the snow-dusted heights overlooking the foothills, Growless Cave serves primarily as a den for the territorial mountain yetis that roam Alterac. Travelers navigating the treacherous slopes often steer clear of its mouth, especially when the notorious yeti Skhowl is sighted prowling outside. Beyond the primal danger of the beasts, the cave harbors a sinister past: inside lies the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left behind by the ambitious human mage Helcular. Before his demise, Helcular intended to use the pyre in a dark ritual to achieve lichdom, and its foul warmth once drew the massive predator Frostmaw out from the frozen wastes.

subzone:gurubashi-arena.text: Gurubashi Arena. Gurubashi Arena is an ancient stone colosseum standing in southern Stranglethorn Vale, originally built by the mighty Gurubashi Empire. In the present day, it serves as a chaotic free-for-all proving ground where pirates and wandering brawlers shed blood over locked chests of treasure. Long before human or orc set foot in Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi Arena—known also as the Great Arena—was built as a monument to martial strength by the sprawling Gurubashi troll empire. In ancient days, champions fought to the death upon its sands until the earth was slick with troll blood. Though the empire has long since fractured into warring tribes, the arena's floor never stays clean for long. Today, lawless buccaneers and ruffians oversee a different sort of bloody spectacle. A pirate named Short John Mithril oversees the grounds, where every few hours a chest of plundered booty is hauled into the center of the ring. Anyone who steps onto the floor is fair game—faction allegiances vanish, and combatants must butcher their way to the prize against all comers.

subzone:hall-of-masks.text: Hall of Masks. The Hall of Masks is an ominous chamber inside the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with giant skull masks and marred by a bone-strewn trench, it marks one of the early thresholds deeper into the Atal'ai stronghold. Located just past the staircase descending from the Broken Hall, the Hall of Masks serves as a central junction within the Sunken Temple. The chamber earns its name from the imposing, stylized skull masks mounted along its stone walls. Below them runs a deep trench choked with discarded bones, suggesting a macabre purpose whose exact nature is unknown. Beyond this eerie hall lie passages branching out to the Butchery, the Chamber of Blood, and the Den of the Caller.

subzone:hammerfall.text: Hammerfall. Hammerfall is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in the Arathi Highlands, built upon the ruins of a notorious Alliance internment camp. It honors the legendary former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell nearby while fighting to liberate his captive people. Today, orcs and Forsaken garrison the settlement against hostile Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark trolls, and the League of Arathor. Following the Second War, the human Alliance built vast internment camps across Lordaeron to contain the defeated orcs. The compound that once stood here was among the largest. Years later, Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer assaulted the camp to liberate the lethargic captives. During the chaos of their retreat, a charging Alliance knight drove a lance through Doomhammer's backplate, mortally wounding the legendary Warchief. Following the Third War, the new Horde reclaimed the ruined ground and established an outpost here, naming it Hammerfall in memory of their fallen leader. Today, Hammerfall serves as the Horde's lifeline in Arathi. Positioned against hostile surroundings, the garrison contends with aggressive Boulderfist ogres from Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall, as well as the native Witherbark trolls. Furthermore, Forsaken Defilers have made the outpost their staging ground to claim the contested resources of the Arathi Basin against the Alliance's League of Arathor.

subzone:harborage.text: Harborage. The Harborage is a quiet settlement of exiled Draenor natives situated in the northern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. While many of their afflicted kin wandering the surrounding bogs have succumbed to madness and primal hostility, the inhabitants here have managed to hold onto their sanity and wits. They live cautiously along the waterline, seeking peace amidst a harsh and unforgiving wilderness. Tucked away against the northern mountains of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Harborage stands in stark contrast to the feral tribes wandering the nearby waters. Constructed of rugged leather shelters and adorned with mysterious hanging crystals, this small encampment provides sanctuary to exiled Draenor survivors who have refused to surrender their minds. Under the guidance of elders like Magtoor, they maintain a fragile, civilized enclave while remaining watchful of the hostile wilderness, native predators, and the feral tribes of their fallen brothers lurking just beyond their perimeter.

subzone:hetaera-s-clutch.text: Hetaera's Clutch. Hetaera's Clutch is a sunken night elven temple dedicated to Elune, nestled deep beneath the churning waters of Azshara's Bay of Storms. Once a sacred site of devotion, the submerged ruins are now overrun by deadly hydras hatched by their broodmother, Hetaera. Adventurers braving the depths will find ancient stonework claimed by vicious aquatic predators. Before the Great Sundering tore ancient Kalimdor apart, this structure served as a grand temple dedicated to the moon goddess Elune. Cast into the depths of the Bay of Storms, its stone pillars and sacred halls have spent ten thousand years beneath the sea. Today, all signs of holy veneration have been swallowed by the tides, leaving behind a solemn monument to the lost Kaldorei empire. The submerged sanctuary has taken on a far deadlier identity as the nesting ground of Hetaera, a massive multi-headed hydra who stalks the nearby coastal waters and rocky isles. Her numerous offspring, the Spawn of Hetaera, prowl through the ruined arches and corridors of the drowned temple, attacking any surface-dweller bold enough to dive into the bay.

subzone:high-wilderness.text: High Wilderness. The High Wilderness is an expansive, untamed stretch of primordial forest covering much of western Feralas. Bordered by the Verdantis River to the east and the Forgotten Coast to the west, it shelters a wide array of wildlife, wandering treants, and dangerous beasts beneath its towering emerald canopy. Stretching across the western half of Feralas, the High Wilderness represents the quintessential untamed wilderness of southern Kalimdor. Thick foliage and colossal trees block out much of the sky, creating a lush expanse teeming with wolves, bears, hippogryphs, and yetis. Ancient treants wander among the roots, while aggressive ogre clans establish footholds in the shaded clearings. Navigating this vast green expanse requires vigilance, as the dense brush hides both natural predators and lingering primeval hazards.

subzone:horizon-scout.text: Horizon Scout. The Horizon Scout is a sunken vessel resting on the ocean floor in the Ruined Reaches off the southern coast of Azshara. While its captain remains stranded ashore, several crew members remain trapped in the submerged hull, kept alive beneath the waves by an arcane water-breathing enchantment. Resting beneath the waves among the treacherous shoals of the Ruined Reaches, the Horizon Scout met a violent end off Azshara's jagged coast. While Captain Vanessa Beltis managed to reach land on a nearby peninsula, a portion of the crew went down with the hull. Miraculously, the survivors inside have not drowned; a gnome named Roland Geardabbler maintains a sustained magical bubble of water breathing that preserves them within the wreckage. Surrounded by hostile aquatic predators and predatory naga, the remaining sailors wait in the dark forward compartments, unable to surface on their own. Evidence aboard the ship hints at the sinister forces behind its destruction. In the forward stairwell lies a small shard of raw Azsharite, a mysterious mineral unique to these shores. The Spitelash naga prowling the waters around the Ruined Reaches likely struck the Horizon Scout to plunder whatever artifacts or resources the expedition carried, dragging the vessel down to ensure no survivors could escape with secrets or treasures of the coast.

subzone:ironstone-camp.text: Ironstone Camp. Ironstone Camp is an outpost established by the Horde along the western border of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Originally deployed to expel Alliance dwarven excavators from the nearby digsite, the encampment's forces now face a deadly threat after subterranean silithid overran the excavation. Ironstone Camp sits directly on the threshold between the high pillars of Thousand Needles and the blazing salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats. The Horde detachment stationed here was initially dispatched with a clear and singular objective: dislodge the dwarven excavators digging at the Rustmaul Digsite. However, their military confrontation was cut short when a swarm of voracious silithid burst forth from a nearby cavern, violently engulfing the dig and attacking both sides. Led by Moktar Krin, the surviving camp defenders have diverted their efforts to combating the insectoid infestation before the swarm spreads unchecked across the region.

subzone:irontree-woods.text: Irontree Woods. Irontree Woods is a blighted grove situated in northern Felwood, once cherished by the night elves as a peaceful forest sanctuary. Ravaged by the demonic corruption of the Third War, its ancient protectors have been petrified into stone while twisted treants and elementals prowl among the ruins. Irontree Woods was once a tranquil woodland glade tended by the kaldorei, but the demonic taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War choked the life from its soil. The grove's guardian Ancients—Hastat, Stoma, and Vartrus—succumbed to the dark magic, petrifying into lifeless stone monuments that still stand entombed amid the corrupted brush. Now, maddened treants, vile bog beasts, and tainted water elementals wander the twisted forest floor, striking violently at any travelers who dare approach.

subzone:isle-of-dread.text: Isle of Dread. The Isle of Dread is a desolate, cliff-bound island situated in the Great Sea off the southwestern coast of Feralas, south of Sardor Isle. It is notorious for sheltering monstrous two-headed chimaeroks and an entrenched coven of hostile naga hidden within its subterranean sea caves. Rising out of the crashing surf of the South Seas, the Isle of Dread lives up to its ominous name. Ringed by sheer cliffs, the island's interior valley is only accessible through a narrow pathway on its southeastern coast. Within this enclosed highland roams a lethal population of chimaeroks—ravenous, two-headed beasts empowered by ambient arcane energies. These beasts are led by the monstrous Lord Lakmaeran, making the island a deadly deathtrap for unwary explorers who cross the channel from Sardor Isle. While the inland plateau belongs to the chimaeroks, the island's northern shore conceals a cavern system occupied by the Hatecrest naga. Led by Lord Shalzaru, these serpent-folk lurk within deep submerged chambers, plotting against the night elven sentinels stationed at nearby Feathermoon Stronghold. Their subterranean lair includes hidden underwater passages that wind into secluded grottoes, serving as a heavily fortified outpost away from mainland scrutiny.

subzone:jadefire-run.text: Jadefire Run. Jadefire Run is a heavily fortified satyr encampment nestled in northern Felwood. It houses some of the most powerful and cunning satyrs in the region, serving as a bastion of demonic corruption deep within the tainted forest. Situated amid the blighted woods of northern Felwood, Jadefire Run functions as a stronghold for the Jadefire satyrs. Unlike lesser outposts scattered throughout the valley, this camp features substantial demonic construction and shelters formidable spellcasters and tricksters. The satyrs here actively conspire to spread corruption further across Kalimdor, employing dark sorcery and foul trickery against anyone who dares intrude on their territory.

subzone:jaedenar.text: Jaedenar. Jaedenar is a blighted hollow in central Felwood built over ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens. Named in foul homage to the demon lord Kil'jaeden, it serves as the primary base of operations for the Shadow Council in northern Kalimdor. Cultists, warlocks, and summoned demons scour the corrupt hollow, guarding the subterranean descent into the Shadow Hold. Long ago, these hollows sheltered night elf sacred grounds and slumbering druids connected to the Emerald Dream. After the devastation of the Third War, the vile remnant of the Shadow Council laid claim to the valley, christening it Jaedenar to honor the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Warlocks—predominantly renegade orcs and Forsaken—have gathered here alongside satyrs, succubi, and felguards. They occupy both the surface ruins and the deeper barrow dens, twisting what was once holy woodland into a grim center of demonic invocation. Above ground, the cultists gather at profane sites like the Shrine of the Deceiver, burning braziers of fell flame and conducting rituals to further corrupt the timberland. Beneath the surface lies the entrance to the Shadow Hold, the subterranean stronghold where the council's true masters direct their operations across Felwood. The Emerald Sanctuary watches the festering enclave with profound concern, regularly enlisting daring wanderers to disrupt their summoning circles and douse the dark flames that seal their tunnels.

subzone:jagged-reef.text: Jagged Reef. The Jagged Reef forms the rugged northern coast of Azshara, where sandy beaches meet jagged stone spurs and churning surf. Treacherous rocks lurk beneath the shallow water, making maritime travel impossible. The desolate shore is primarily populated by prowling hydras, scavenging makrura, and territorial murloc tribes. Stretching across Azshara's northern edge, the Jagged Reef is a harsh littoral expanse where broken cliffs and jutting stone outcroppings divide the sandy shores into secluded inlets. Beneath the breaking waves lie submerged crags and shifting shallows, turning the waters into a graveyard for any vessel foolish enough to venture near. On land, the wild coastline offers little comfort; salt-crusted beasts, predatory hydras, and aggressive makrura wander the surf line alongside entrenched murlocs scouring the tides for scraps and unwary prey.

subzone:jaguero-isle.text: Jaguero Isle. Jaguero Isle is an isolated, jungle-covered island resting off the eastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale's Wild Shore. Dominated by fierce wild panthers and gorillas, it is infamous as the domain of the colossal silverback gorilla known as King Mukla. Situated off the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, Jaguero Isle stands well apart from the mainland pirate camps and troll ruins. The island is entirely overrun by untamed fauna, mainly panthers and aggressive gorillas. Looming over them all is the gargantuan ape King Mukla, whose rule over the rocky interior is absolute and territorial. Few sailors willingly approach its reefs, though occasionally washed-up bottles along the mainland beaches carry desperate pleas for rescue from those unfortunate enough to be stranded ashore.

subzone:janeiro-s-point.text: Janeiro's Point. Janeiro's Point is a small, rocky island situated just outside the harbor of Booty Bay in southern Stranglethorn Vale. It is crowned by a colossal stone statue of an unknown goblin welcoming incoming maritime traffic with outstretched arms. The island's waters and shores are dominated by the menacing sea giant known as Mok'rash the Cleaver. Standing as the monumental gateway to Booty Bay, Janeiro's Point greets every vessel charting a course into the southern seas of Stranglethorn Vale. Atop the crag looms an immense stone effigy of a goblin, arms spread wide in a grand gesture of welcome and unbridled mercantile ambition. Though visible to sailors and corsairs for miles around, landing on the island's shores is a perilous prospect due to Mok'rash the Cleaver, a terrifying sea giant who has claimed the outcrop as his territory.

subzone:kargath.text: Kargath. Kargath is a fortified Horde outpost perched in the western Badlands, serving as their sole foothold in Khaz Modan. Established by the Kargath Expeditionary Force under Warchief Thrall's orders, the settlement anchors crucial transit lines across the Eastern Kingdoms while staging operations toward Blackrock Mountain and the excavation at Uldaman. Named in honor of the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, the outpost of Kargath stands as the Horde's solitary settlement throughout the mountain realms of Khaz Modan. Surrounded by arid wastes, aggressive wildlife, and hostile dwarven factions, the garrison provides a vital midway sanctuary for travelers crossing the continent. Its flight master bridges the long divide between northern holdings like the Undercity and Hammerfall and southern redoubts like Stonard and Grom'gol Base Camp. Dispatched on direct orders from Warchief Thrall, the Kargath Expeditionary Force maintains a dual objective in the region. Troops make frequent forays into the ancient titan halls of Uldaman to uncover why Ironforge's Prospectors prize the dig site so dearly. Concurrently, scouts labor to carve a path through the Searing Gorge into Blackrock Mountain, seeking to strike at Rend Blackhand's false 'Dark Horde' while contending with the entrenched Dark Iron dwarves.

subzone:kodo-graveyard.text: Kodo Graveyard. The Kodo Graveyard is a sprawling expanse in central Desolace littered with the massive, bleached remains of ancient beasts. By instinct or tradition, aging and dying kodos make a final pilgrimage to this desolate hollow to collapse among the ribs of their ancestors. Sprawling across the grey earth of Desolace, the Kodo Graveyard holds the colossal skeletons of ancient beasts, some far larger than any living kodo seen today. Dying kodos wander here to spend their final breaths among centuries of accumulated remains. This sacred peace is fragile: scavengers prowl the perimeter, and those who disturb the calcified ribs and skulls risk stirring furious kodo spirits from the dust. The boundary between the living and the dead wears exceptionally thin across the bone fields. Travelers who peer into the spirit realm find restless, towering kodo apparitions wandering silently among the dust storms. Nearby, the Horde maintains Ghost Walker Post, watching over the sacred grounds and keeping a wary eye on the wandering herds and spectral manifestations that linger around the bones.

subzone:kormek-s-hut.text: Kormek's Hut. Kormek's Hut is a remote, ramshackle dwelling sitting amid the barren flats of north-central Desolace. Despite its desolate surroundings and mysterious namesake, it currently shelters an eccentric pair: an oddly peaceful cultist and a goblin obsessed with harvesting kodo bones. Perched out in the arid wastes of north-central Desolace, this small hovel is named after a figure whose whereabouts and identity remain completely unknown. Instead of Kormek, travelers stumbling upon the hut encounter an unusual pairing living out in the middle of nowhere: Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle. Inside the hut sits Willow, a member of the otherwise hostile and nihilistic Twilight's Hammer who curiously treats outsiders with calm hospitality. Outside, a pen littered with sun-bleached kodo bones serves as the personal dance floor and staging ground for Bibbly, an excitable goblin captivated by the commercial potential of bone scavenging.

subzone:kurzen-s-compound.text: Kurzen's Compound. Kurzen's Compound is a heavily fortified human settlement tucked into the hills of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Established by an expedition dispatched from Stormwind under Colonel Kurzen, the outpost has devolved into a rogue camp of cutthroats and wild beasts following their commander's descent into madness. What began as an official expedition into the untamed jungles of Stranglethorn turned into a nightmare when Colonel Kurzen lost his mind. Rather than fulfilling Stormwind's mission, the garrison broke away from the kingdom's authority, cutting ties with the crown and descending into tyranny. Today, the compound operates like a mercenary stronghold, complete with a functional lumber mill, stables for training captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers as weapons of war, and an extensive cave complex known as the Stockpile where the rogue soldiers stash their plundered supplies. Not all of the expedition's original members followed their commander into savagery. When Kurzen's madness took hold, a faction of his men mutinied and fled west to form the Rebel Camp, sparking a bitter and bloody feud within the dense canopy. From their fortified compound, Kurzen and his loyal men ruthlessly hunt down the deserters, treating any outsider who steps into their jungle domain as an enemy of the expedition.

subzone:lake-mennar.text: Lake Mennar. Lake Mennar is a tranquil body of freshwater nestled amidst the shattered ruins of Azshara. It is remarkably renowned as one of the exceedingly rare havens outside of Northrend where members of the blue dragonflight reside. While the perimeter teems with protective blue dragonspawn, the shores of the lake itself remain strangely serene. Situated in the ancient, broken landscape of Azshara, Lake Mennar serves as a secluded gathering ground for the blue dragonflight. Aside from Mazthoril to the north in Winterspring, it is virtually unheard of to encounter blue dragons in such numbers across Kalimdor. Blue dragonspawn tirelessly patrol the ridges and approaches circling the basin, fiercely guarding the waters. Yet for any wanderer daring enough to slip through this vigilant ring of sentries, the calm waters of the lake offer unexpected quietude, shielded from the arcane turmoil and roaming beast packs common to the rest of the peninsula.

subzone:lake-nazferiti.text: Lake Nazferiti. Lake Nazferiti is a sprawling freshwater lake nestled in the dense jungle of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Fed by a vast river system stretching far north into the mountains, its waters are infested with ferocious crocolisks and snapping frenzies, while its shores host an industrial encampment operated by the goblin Venture Company. Lake Nazferiti sits along the Nazferiti River, one of the longest continuous waterways across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. The river traces its origins deep into the northern heights, tumbling down waterfalls from the Redridge Mountains and possibly originating as far inland as Deadwind Pass. Within Stranglethorn, the water widens into this murky lake, teeming with vicious predators like snapping river frenzies and ambush-hunting crocolisks that make casual swimming deadly. The natural balance of Lake Nazferiti is under siege by the goblins of the Venture Company. Setting up heavy operations along the lake's banks, these ruthless profiteers exploit the jungle's timber and resources with mechanical saws, drills, and clear-cutting crews. Their sprawling base pollutes the waterways and constantly clashes with local wildlife and wandering hunters braving the vale.

subzone:lakkari-tar-pits.text: Lakkari Tar Pits. The Lakkari Tar Pits are a series of foul-smelling, bubbling pools of thick black sludge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Situated just below the cliffs of Marshal's Refuge, they act as a natural death trap for unwary beasts and an incubator for hostile tar elementals. The Lakkari Tar Pits dominate the low ground of northern Un'Goro Crater, directly south of Marshal's Refuge. Thick, reeking pools of pitch entrap anything careless enough to step into them, quickly bogging down beasts and adventurers alike. The protruding bones of hundreds of prehistoric creatures break the black surface, bearing witness to generations of animals sucked into the mire. Opportunistic scavengers circle the margins waiting for trapped prey to exhaust itself, while living tar beasts, lurkers, and creepers rise directly from the muck to batter interlopers.

subzone:land-s-end-beach.text: Land's End Beach. Land's End Beach is a desolate stretch of coastline at the far southern tip of Tanaris, effectively marking the southern edge of Kalimdor. Shielded by towering mountain ridges and vast ocean waters, it remains one of the most secluded and inaccessible shores on the continent. Tucked away behind the southern mountain ranges of Tanaris and the sealed titan gateway to Uldum, Land's End Beach represents the absolute southern edge of Kalimdor's mainland. Cut off from overland routes across the desert dunes, reaching this windswept coast requires swimming along the dangerous, fatigue-inducing open waters of the South Seas. The beach is a barren frontier of crashing surf, shifting sand, and quiet isolation, largely untamed by the cartels or desert explorers who dwell farther north around Gadgetzan. Beyond the breakers of the beach lie lonely, unnamed islets separated from the mainland by vast expanses of exhausting deep water. Navigating to these distant specks of rock is treacherous enough to push even seasoned swimmers to their physical limits. Few mortals have any reason to seek out the lonely waters at Kalimdor's end, leaving the beach and its surrounding shoals undisturbed beneath the blazing southern sun.

subzone:lariss-pavilion.text: Lariss Pavilion. Lariss Pavilion is an ancient elven structure tucked into the wilderness of Feralas just north of Camp Mojache. While once a peaceful retreat of classical night elf architecture, the surrounding forest has grown dangerous due to corrupted dryads, and an exiled Highborne mage now bides his time within its shade. Standing quietly on the bluffs north of Camp Mojache, Lariss Pavilion showcases the graceful stonework and towering archways of the ancient kaldorei empire. In its prime, it served the great city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Today, it offers a sheltered overlook above the dense canopy of Feralas, but the peace here is frail: the once-gentle dryads wandering the surrounding glades have fallen to madness and corruption, turning fiercely hostile to anyone who draws near. The pavilion's most notable resident is the elusive elf Azj'Tordin. Having broken away from Prince Tortheldrin's decadent rule within Dire Maul, Azj'Tordin escaped the ruins through a secret passage connecting the pavilion directly to the ancient city's underbelly. However, his quiet exile has been disrupted: an erratic imp named Pusillin stole his treasured book of incantations, leaving the exile seeking outside aid to recover it.

subzone:launch-bay.text: Launch Bay. The Launch Bay is a subterranean airfield and hangar tucked within the depths of Gnomeregan, located just beyond the Hall of Gears. Once the staging ground for gnomish flying machines and bombers, it has fallen completely under the control of hostile leper gnomes and corrupted mechanical contraptions. Serving as the primary hangar for Gnomeregan's aerial fleet, the Launch Bay is split across two tiers. Its central platform, reached by ramps from the upper walkway, still houses parked gnomish flying machines and heavy bombers that never made it out before the city was evacuated. Instead of skilled pilots, the flight decks are now crawling with crazed leper gnomes who maintain and guard the idling war machines. Beyond its military role, the Launch Bay serves as a vital junction within the complex. Ramps from its southeastern corridor descend into the Engineering Labs, while a southern passage on the lower deck is choked with invading Dark Iron dwarves. That southern tunnel provides a perilous path toward the heart of the city at Tinkers' Court.

subzone:lethlor-ravine.text: Lethlor Ravine. Lethlor Ravine is a jagged, rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Badlands. It serves as a perilous roost and breeding ground for the black dragonflight, swarming with aggressive whelps and mature drakes. Carved deep into the scorched plateaus of the eastern Badlands, Lethlor Ravine is one of the most hazardous stretches of the desert. The craggy canyon walls provide a natural aerie for the black dragonflight, housing nests of fierce dragon whelps guarded by larger, fire-breathing drakes. Few travelers dare approach the valley floor, as the shadows overhead constantly betray the flight of winged predators circling among the rocky spires. Beyond the scaly brood that claims it, Lethlor Ravine is marked by curious crystalline obelisks scattered throughout the crags. These crystalline formations are involved in a local quest chain. Their origin is not established.

subzone:loading-room.text: Loading Room. The Loading Room is an industrial staging chamber inside Gnomeregan's sprawling mechanical complex. In the current era, this subterranean staging area lies deep within the corrupted fallen capital, dangerously close to rogue constructs such as Techbot. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the Loading Room functioned as a bustling transit point and cargo staging bay linked to the subterranean transit networks of the tinker capital. Today, like the rest of the ruined city, it has succumbed to chaos. Radioactive fallout, invading troggs, and malfunctioning machinery have rendered the area extremely perilous. The rogue mechanized construct Techbot guards the vicinity, posing a severe threat to any gnome survivors or daring Alliance reclaimers attempting to secure the perimeter.

subzone:lost-point.text: Lost Point. Lost Point is a dilapidated wooden watchtower standing in western Dustwallow Marsh, originally constructed by Theramore's forces as an advance scout post. It has since fallen into disrepair and slipped from the control of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's guard, now serving as a hideout for rogue deserters. Erected by the expeditionary forces of Theramore to monitor traffic and threats emerging from the Barrens, Lost Point has long outlived its intended military function. The outpost has decayed under the relentless moisture of the marsh, its timber rotting and its defenses abandoned by regular troops. Instead of garrison sentries, the tower and its immediate surroundings are occupied by human deserters who broke away from Theramore's service, finding shelter in the isolated wilderness far from the discipline of the city's commanders.

subzone:lost-rigger-cove.text: Lost Rigger Cove. Tucked away along the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, Lost Rigger Cove serves as the primary base of operations for the Southsea Pirates in the region. Shielded by towering desert mountains on three sides, this hidden port boasts docks, fortified encampments, and an active shipyard constructing new pirate vessels. Naturally fortified by sheer rock walls on almost every side, Lost Rigger Cove provides the Southsea Freebooters an ideal maritime stronghold on Kalimdor's southeastern edge. Here, pirate cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands haul salvage and assemble fresh hulls right under the noses of Gadgetzan's authorities. The cove allows the Southseas to project power across the Great Sea while raiding trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements. The pirates do not hold their cove unchallenged. The goblins of Gadgetzan and nearby Steamwheedle Port resent the raiders on their doorstep and pay mercenaries to slaughter the Southseas, thin their ranks, and disrupt their operations.

subzone:lower-wilds.text: Lower Wilds. The Lower Wilds form the eastern threshold of Feralas, where the humid forests meet the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. The main road cutting through these woods connects Thalanaar at the border to the settlements further west, flanked by ancient greenery and unpredictable woodland creatures. Spanning the eastern reaches of Feralas, the Lower Wilds serve as the natural transition between the sun-baked ravines of Thousand Needles and the deep, primordial jungle to the west. Travelers entering the zone must traverse this stretch of forest along the main highway, past the elven outpost of Thalanaar guarding the mountain pass. The dense canopies here house ancient treants, alongside indigenous wildlife that makes straying from the beaten path perilous. Because it links the southern wilderness to the eastern territories, the Lower Wilds see frequent movement of travelers, scouts, and couriers. While the night elves hold the gateway at Thalanaar, the Horde maintains Camp Mojache further inland. The road winding through the Lower Wilds is therefore a critical lifeline for anyone moving supplies across southern Kalimdor, fraught with both nature's hazards and faction tensions.

subzone:magram-village.text: Magram Village. Magram Village is the settlement of the Magram centaur clan, situated among foul yellow pools in southeastern Desolace. It serves as the primary base for the Magram as they wage relentless war against their hated rivals, the Gelkis. Sprawled across islands and shores around stagnant, sulfurous pools in southeast Desolace, Magram Village is a rugged settlement cobbled together with crude wooden bridges and hide tents. The Magram centaur dwell here in constant vigilance against neighboring clans. Known for their sheer brutality and deep-seated animosity toward the southern Gelkis clan, the Magram are willing to tolerate outsiders only if those travelers prove their worth by slaughtering their Gelkis enemies.

subzone:maker-s-terrace.text: Maker's Terrace. The Maker's Terrace is a sprawling outdoor excavation site situated in the northern Badlands, directly fronting the entrance to the ancient titan vault of Uldaman. Travelers venturing south from Loch Modan must navigate its rugged perimeter, which is aggressively occupied by Dark Iron dwarves. The dig represents a contested threshold between the surface wastes and the titan mysteries entombed below. Sprawling across the northern bluffs of the Badlands, the Maker's Terrace serves as the exterior staging ground for the subterranean halls of Uldaman. Long before travelers delve into the subterranean ruins, they must contend with the sun-scorched earthworks, scaffolding, and stone trenches of this grand excavation. It sits right along the pass coming down from Loch Modan, making it the first landmark greeting any traveler daring to venture into the arid wastes. The Terrace buzzes with violent industry as rival factions seek a way into the ancient secrets buried beneath the rock. The site is firmly under the boot of the Dark Iron clan, who patrol its ditches and perimeters with hostile vigilance. Drawn by the scent of titan relics and subterranean dominance, these subterranean dwarves dig incessantly into the hillside, seeking whatever armaments, records, or earthen relics the ancient Makers left behind. Anyone trying to reach the deep halls of Uldaman without clearing through these fortified sentries will quickly find themselves overwhelmed.

subzone:mannoroc-coven.text: Mannoroc Coven. Mannoroc Coven is a demon-infested ruin in southern Desolace, named after the pit lord Mannoroth. Settled among ancient night elf architecture, it stands as the largest stronghold of the Burning Legion in central Kalimdor. Cultists of the Burning Blade maintain active summoning portals here, filling the ash-choked land with felhounds, succubi, and infernals. Situated south of Ghost Walker Post and east of Shadowprey Village, Mannoroc Coven blankets the ancient night elf ruins in an oppressive, fel-tainted pall. The coven is commanded on the ground by Lord Azrethoc, alongside the Burning Blade warlock Jugkar Grim'rod. Together, they harness active summoning portals to pull demonic reinforcements straight into Kalimdor, including doomguards, infernals, and felhounds. Even as Horde-aligned travelers attempt to sever these links using relics like the Hand of Iruxos, new rifts continue to tear open through the scarred earth.

subzone:maul-subzone.text: Maul (subzone). The Maul is a sunken fighting arena situated in the Broken Commons outside the ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Formerly a grand venue of ancient elven Eldre'Thalas, the pit is now an uncontrolled bloodsport ring where wanderers fight for glory or survival against fierce beasts and rival champions. Carved deep into the stone of the Broken Commons, the Maul once served the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas as a theater or ceremonial arena. Following the Sundering and the subsequent occupation by the Gordok ogres, the pit devolved into a raw colosseum. Like the notorious Gurubashi Arena in distant Stranglethorn Vale, entering the sands of the Maul suspends all allegiances, casting combatants into a lawless free-for-all where faction lines dissolve and survival depends purely on martial strength. Challengers who descend into the arena must mind their approach. While daring fighters often leap directly from the high ledges of the commons, the fall carries brutal impact. A safer western archway leads through tunnels lined with slumbering Gordok hyenas, providing the only foot exit out of the fighting floor. At irregular intervals, dangerous beasts and notorious gladiators emerge into the pit, making every descent an unpredictable trial of steel and instinct.

subzone:menethil-bay.text: Menethil Bay. Menethil Bay is the sheltered body of water along the western coast of the Wetlands, nestled between Menethil Harbor and the steep northern cliffs of Dun Morogh. Opening outward into the wider Baradin Bay, these waters are home to aggressive crocolisks and the remains of sunken vessels. It serves as the primary maritime approach for Alliance traffic journeying between the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Part of the larger Baradin Bay along the Great Sea, Menethil Bay forms a natural inlet bordered by Menethil Harbor to the north, Black Channel Marsh to the east, and the towering coastal bluffs of Dun Morogh to the south. Its shallow margins and marshy shores crawl with crocolisks of various ages and sizes, making the shallows treacherous for unguided travelers even though the bay serves as the lifeblood of Alliance maritime travel. Near the mouth of the bay lies the ruined wreckage of the Flying Osprey, a silent reminder of the dangers lurking beneath the surface.

subzone:menethil-keep.text: Menethil Keep. Menethil Keep is the stone stronghold dominating the skyline of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Marked by four sturdy watchtowers, it serves as the administrative heart and defensive bastion of the Alliance port, housing the local militia commander, Captain Stoutfist. Rising above the wooden docks and soggy marshes of the Wetlands, Menethil Keep is the central military strongpoint of Menethil Harbor. With four stone watchtowers gazing out over the town and the bay, the fortress offers a commanding view against seaward raiders, renegades, and the encroaching swamp beasts. Inside, Captain Stoutfist oversees the defense of the port, directing the town militia and organizing patrols to safeguard Alliance interests throughout the region.

subzone:mirage-flats.text: Mirage Flats. Mirage Flats is a barren, sun-scorched expanse nestled in the central wastes of the Badlands. Lying east of Dustbelch Grotto, this dry plateau is notorious for shimmering heat hazes and hungry predators. Situated east of Dustbelch Grotto, the Mirage Flats present travelers with an unforgiving stretch of cracked red dirt and shimmering heat waves that give the plain its name. Few civilized souls linger here; instead, the open flats are dominated by opportunistic scavengers and lethal beasts. Flocks of giant buzzards circle lazily on hot thermals above, watching for the leavings of ferocious ridge stalkers and pack-hunting crag coyotes that scour the brush for easy prey.

subzone:misty-reed-post.text: Misty Reed Post. Misty Reed Post is a rugged Horde encampment situated between Stagalbog and the Misty Reed Strand in the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Established as a frontline watch under the authority of Stonard, it serves to monitor the dangerous wetlands and the treacherous coastline. Tucked away in the humid gloom between the Stagalbog and the eastern shore, Misty Reed Post is little more than a spartan camp under Stonard's banner. It is manned by a handful of Stonard hunters, a shaman, Katar, and Tok'Kar, who oversees the watch. Conditions are rough, offering no fortified shelter from the marsh's hostile wildlife and lingering damp. Tok'Kar harbors quiet ambitions that the Horde command in Stonard will one day reinforce the position with a sturdy orcish burrow or watchtower, though for now, the scouts must hold the marsh with tents, campfire smoke, and sharpened steel.

subzone:misty-shore.text: Misty Shore. Misty Shore is the quiet lakeshore of the Alterac Mountains, skirting the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Stretching between Dandred's Fold and the perimeter of Dalaran, it offers wide, foggy views of the Dawning Isles and the sinister silhouette of Fenris Keep. Running along Lordamere Lake, the Misty Shore stretches between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Thick, damp air regularly drifts off the lake, obscuring snapping turtles and the occasional zealous fanatic who wanders down from regional strongholds. From the banks of the Misty Shore, travelers look out across the waters toward the Dawning Isles and the imposing shadow of Fenris Keep. Because of its vantage point across Lordamere Lake and its proximity to both Dalaran and Scarlet-controlled pockets, travelers along the bank often keep a low profile to avoid unwanted attention.

subzone:misty-valley.text: Misty Valley. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Valley is a shadowed, fog-drenched hollow north of the pass into Deadwind. The secluded basin is overrun by primordial swamp beasts, wandering swampwalkers, and tangled horrors. Deep in its rearmost cave dwells the colossal and terrifying Mire Lord. Nestled beneath the high cliffs separating the Swamp of Sorrows from Deadwind Pass, the Misty Valley is perpetually choked with thick marsh vapor. Unlike the open wetlands to the east, this isolated pocket is dense with colossal marsh elementals, including looming swampwalkers, ancient swampwalker elders, and creeping tangled horrors. At the far end of the misty gorge lies a cavern that serves as the lair of the Mire Lord, one of the most formidable natural threats haunting the bog.

subzone:mizjah-ruins.text: Mizjah Ruins. The Mizjah Ruins are ancient stone remains nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long abandoned by their original troll architects, the crumbling structures have been seized by the brute-strength Mosh'Ogg ogres. From this vantage, the ogres launch disruptive ambushes against passing supply caravans traveling toward the Swamp of Sorrows. Like many of the ancient stone ruins scattered throughout Stranglethorn Vale, the Mizjah Ruins were built by the Gurubashi Empire long before modern empires rose. Today, the moss-choked arches and cracked flagstones are occupied by the Mosh'Ogg clan, primarily brute warriors and crude witch doctors. Far from keeping to their stolen perimeter, these ogres routinely raid nearby supply convoys bound for the Horde settlement of Stonard, transforming ancient history into a persistent, bloody thorn in the side of Grom'gol's commanders.

subzone:morlos-aran.text: Morlos'Aran. Morlos'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in the southern reaches of Felwood. Once a proud and thriving settlement before the Great Sundering, it now stands as a grim monument to a lost golden age, drowned under the demonic blight that plagues the surrounding forest. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand urban center of the ancient kaldorei civilization. Much like sister settlements such as Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas bustled with elven life and arcana. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the city broke, leaving only shattered colonnades behind as monuments to their civilization's zenith. While neighboring ruins in Darkshore and Ashenvale fell to decay and wilderness, Morlos'Aran met a far grimmer fate during the Third War. Positioned directly within the corridor trampled by the Burning Legion, its surviving foundations were choked by demonic corruption and toxic mire. Today, the ruins are haunted by wandering beasts, corrupted elementals, and remnants of the shadow forces lingering in Felwood.

subzone:mosh-ogg-ogre-mound.text: Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a fortified cavern complex in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just south of the ruins of Zul'Gurub. It serves as the primary stronghold for the brute Mosh'Ogg tribe in the jungle, dominated by their ruthless ogre mage chieftain, Mai'Zoth. Carved into the rugged jungle ridges south of Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound swarms with brutish Mosh'Ogg maulers, shamans, and warmongers. The ogres seized the cavernous network as an ideal redoubt against hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts. Deep within the twisting interior of the mound presides Mai'Zoth, the formidable two-headed ogre mage who commands the Mosh'Ogg clan. In his possession is the Mind's Eye, a potent and dangerous arcane relic that enhances his mental and sorcerous grip over his followers. Mai'Zoth's mastery over magic and raw brute force makes entering the deepest reaches of the mound a peril for any traveler braving northern Stranglethorn.

subzone:mosshide-fen.text: Mosshide Fen. Mosshide Fen is a swampy, treacherous tract in the eastern Wetlands overrun by the Mosshide gnoll tribe. Dotted with primitive encampments, it is one of the most perilous regions for travelers venturing off the main trade roads. Sprawling across the murky eastern reaches of the Wetlands, Mosshide Fen serves as the primary domain of the aggressive Mosshide gnolls. The swamp here is dense and tangled, dotted with rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps. Under the vicious command of pack leaders like Gnawbone, the gnolls fiercely guard their muddy claims, readily ambushing and devouring any travelers, scouts, or prospectors foolish enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

subzone:nat-s-landing.text: Nat's Landing. Nat's Landing is a modest fishing outpost nestled along the shores of Dustwallow Bay in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the personal camp and retreat of Nat Pagle, widely regarded as the most famous angler on Azeroth. Adventurers from across the world seek out this humble dock to hone their mastery of the fishing craft. Tucked away southwest of Theramore Isle along the murky waters of Dustwallow Bay, Nat's Landing is little more than a weathered campsite. It consists of a simple canvas tent, drying racks heavy with the day's catch, extra tackle hung from trees, and a rickety wooden pier jutting into the bay. Despite the mists and hazards of the swamp, this quiet patch of shoreline provides the legendary angler Nat Pagle with a solitary place to cast his line and enjoy a quiet drink away from civilization's clamor. Though unassuming at a glance, the landing is an essential stop for aspiring anglers. Fishermen who have exhausted the teachings of standard trainers in Ironforge, Orgrimmar, or elsewhere are directed here to prove their worth directly to Nat. Pagle cares nothing for politics or factional squabbles; any angler who braves the marshland predators to reach his dock must demonstrate patience and skill across the world's most perilous waters to earn his highest instruction.

subzone:nek-mani-wellspring.text: Nek'mani Wellspring. Perched high in the cliffs above the Southern Savage Coast, the Nek'mani Wellspring holds a fountain of remarkably pure holy water. It is renowned as the only pristine source of fresh water found south of Duskwood. However, this sacred site has recently been overrun by hostile naga explorers who jealously guard its flow. The Nek'mani Wellspring sits tucked away in the jagged coastal heights of western Stranglethorn Vale. Dispensing the only untainted freshwater south of Duskwood, the spring is hailed by various scholars and pilgrims as holy. Because differing cultures and traditions each claim its divine waters were blessed uniquely for their own kind, it remains a subject of intense theological fascination. Despite its spiritual renown, peaceful contemplation here is impossible: a vicious contingent of naga has recently seized the basin and guards the waters against all intruders.

subzone:nesingwary-s-expedition.text: Nesingwary's Expedition. Nesingwary's Expedition is a rustic hunting encampment situated in northern Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Lake Nazferiti. Established by the famed dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary, the outpost serves as a staging ground for hunters seeking to test their mettle against the jungle's fiercest predators. Tucked alongside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, this remote encampment is a bustling haven for big game hunters, trackers, and marksmen. Hemet Nesingwary established the camp to stalk the legendary beasts of Stranglethorn Vale, surrounded by seasoned peers like Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot. Guarded by hired marksmen and supplied by neutral vendors, the camp welcomes anyone capable of handling a rifle or bow, regardless of their allegiances, uniting them under the singular pursuit of tracking down the deadliest predators the jungle has to offer. Life in the expedition camp revolves around intense competition and grand tall tales. Hunters are continually challenged to master the tracking and slaying of the jungle's native panthers, raptors, and tigers, culminating in hunts for apex beasts. Aside from the thrill of the chase, the camp contends with its own small logistical disasters, notably the scattering of Nesingwary's sprawling manuscript across the wilds, leaving camp scholars eager to recover every missing chapter.

subzone:nethander-stead.text: Nethander Stead. Nethander Stead is an abandoned farmstead lying along the road just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once a working human farm, it has fallen into ruin and is completely overrun by the Mudsnout gnoll pack. The fields are overgrown with giant white mushrooms known as Mudsnout Blossoms, attracting the interest of Forsaken alchemists. Situated within sight of Southshore's eastern borders, Nethander Stead was once an active piece of the region's agricultural belt. Like much of the eastern foothills, the farm was abandoned as regional security eroded and wild packs moved in. Today, it serves as the sole enclave of the Mudsnout gnolls in the foothills. The brutes dwell among the ruined fences and outbuildings, aggressively driving off any travelers who wander too close to their claimed territory.

subzone:nijel-s-point.text: Nijel's Point. Nijel's Point is a fortified Alliance and Cenarion Circle redoubt perched high on the northern bluffs of Desolace. Tucked safely away from the blighted valleys below, it serves as the sole safe haven for Alliance travelers, researchers, and soldiers navigating the harsh wasteland. Carved into the sheer cliffs bordering the Stonetalon Mountains, Nijel's Point stands well above the gray dust and marauding centaur packs of Desolace. The settlement is held by a detachment of the Stormwind Army under Captain Pentigast, charged with monitoring the violent clan wars that threaten Alliance interests across southern Kalimdor. Its high elevation and narrow access trails make it readily defensible, providing a secure staging ground for couriers, scouts, and griffin riders travelling between Stonetalon Peak, Theramore, and Feathermoon Stronghold. Beyond the Stormwind garrison, the outpost shelters emissaries with distinct and perilous agendas. Keeper Marandis and his dryads use the camp as an operational base to confront Princess Theradras deep within Maraudon, seeking to recover the fallen demigod Zaetar. Even the Scarlet Crusade maintains an emissary here in Brother Anton, who seeks to scour the undead ravaging the valley floor. Despite the bustling presence of soldiers and druids, the identity of Nijel himself remains an ancient mystery lost even to those garrisoned atop the ridge.

subzone:northfold-manor.text: Northfold Manor. Northfold Manor is a dilapidated agricultural estate situated on the northwestern fringes of the Arathi Highlands. Once a prosperous human homestead before the collapse of Stromgarde, the grounds are now occupied by criminal operatives of the Syndicate engaging in unsettling, dark practices. Perched on the rolling highlands near the Thoradin's Wall passage, Northfold Manor once supported the kingdom of Stromgarde. In the chaos following the realm's fracturing, displaced Alteraci nobility and outlaws of the Syndicate claimed the manor house, barn, and fields as an operational base. Instead of tending crops, Syndicate mercenaries, highwaymen, and pathstalkers use the farmstead to stage ambushes along the roads and coordinate their presence across Arathi.

subzone:noxious-lair.text: Noxious Lair. The Noxious Lair is a sunken silithid hive situated in the southwestern deserts of Tanaris, bordering Un'Goro Crater. Once a verdant basin with flowing water, the territory has been infested and drained of its vital resources by the burrowing Centipaar swarm. Now, it stands as an acidic breeding ground filled with swarming insectoids and rich mineral veins. Resting against the western ridges overlooking Un'Goro Crater, the Noxious Lair occupies a depression in the sand that once held a lake or shallow river. When the Centipaar silithid invaded, they consumed the desert's remaining underground moisture and transformed the basin into an encroaching colony. Vast pincers and twitching limbs rise directly from the sand dunes, surrounding subterranean tunnels slick with corrosive insect secretions and clusters of incubating eggs. Subterranean tunnels link the surface entrances to humid, acid-coated breeding chambers beneath the sands. Centipaar workers, tunnelers, wasps, and colossal sandreavers patrol the perimeter, defending their brood from outside threats. Beyond its biological dangers, the upheaval caused by silithid excavation has unearthed deep mineral deposits, creating an unusually diverse hunting and prospecting ground where subterranean ores sit exposed amid the swarming hives.

subzone:oneiros.text: Oneiros. Oneiros is a sprawling expanse of ancient night elven ruins located south of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. Tied intimately to the nearby portals leading toward the realm of Ysera, its moss-covered stones are guarded by elite green dragonkin. Stretching across the dense forest floor of northern Feralas, the crumbling stone arches and column fragments of Oneiros hint at an ancient Kaldorei settlement abandoned millennia ago. In the present day, nature has reclaimed the structures, entwining them with massive roots and verdant overgrowth. Elite guardians of the Green Dragonflight relentlessly patrol the shaded paths and broken plazas, warding mortals away from ancient secrets.

subzone:onyxia-s-lair.text: Onyxia's Lair. Onyxia's Lair is a subterranean cavern located deep within the Wyrmbog of Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the nesting sanctuary and stronghold for Onyxia, broodmother of the black dragonflight. Inside its sweltering, magma-filled chambers, the great dragon watches over clutches of black dragon eggs. Carved into the treacherous mud and petrified wood of the Wyrmbog, the cavern entrance resembles the yawning maw of a dragon. Within, the cool rot of the marsh gives way to intense volcanic heat. Magma seeps from cracks in the obsidian stone, while subterranean tremors routinely shake the ceilings. The central chamber opens into a vast incubator where hundreds of black dragon eggs lie nested amid ash and embers, overseen by flightkin, dragonspawn guards, and Onyxia herself.

subzone:pool-of-tears.text: Pool of Tears. The Pool of Tears is a large, murky lake dominating the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Deep beneath its surface lies the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, brought low by the Green Dragonflight to contain the horrors within. Today, vicious frenzies patrol the turbid waters, and ancient troll ruins litter its drowned banks. Long ago, fanatical Atal'ai trolls raised a monumental ziggurat to their bloodthirsty god, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Horrified by the blasphemies taking place within, the Dragon Aspect Ysera shattered the ground beneath the structure, submerging the massive temple into the depths of the marsh. The existing lake flooded over the temple ruins. While the dragons sought to bury the evil forever, the ziggurat still stands beneath the silt and waves, and green drakes remain vigilant in the area to keep its corruption sealed. Navigating the murky lake is treacherous for any adventurer heading toward the sunken halls. Flesh-eating frenzies infest the waters, while Atal'ai artifacts and drowned stonework remain scattered across the muddy floor. Travelers must brave these hostile shallows to access the upper passages of the submerged temple, where cultists and lingering dragon guardians vie for control of the dark sanctuary.

subzone:quagmire.text: Quagmire. The Quagmire comprises the sprawling, treacherous heart of central Dustwallow Marsh. Bound by Brackenwall Village to the north and the Dragonmurk to the south, its waterlogged flats are notoriously difficult to navigate. Hostile beasts and ravenous oozes make any journey through this central fen perilous. Occupying the wide expanse between Lost Point in the west and Dustwallow Bay in the east, the Quagmire represents the wild core of the marsh. Footing is unreliable at best, with solid earth constantly giving way to murky water and clinging mud. Travelers must contend with predatory crocolisks lurking beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nesting in the dead brush, and strange oozes that seep through the muck. Beyond its natural hazards, the Quagmire serves as an unpredictable crossroads for the sentient powers contesting the swamp. Tucked away within the bog lies Tabetha's Farm, a lonely refuge for practitioners seeking hermit wisdom amid the dangers of the swamp.

subzone:rage-scar-hold.text: Rage Scar Hold. Rage Scar Hold is a cavern carved into the wilderness of Feralas, situated on the mainland not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. It is notorious for housing some of the most vicious yetis in the region. Strangely, scattered books, symbols, and traces of night elven architecture deeper within suggest the den once served a far more civil purpose before the beasts claimed it. Carved into the rugged wilds of Feralas, Rage Scar Hold is dominated by savage yetis that attack anyone venturing near their lair. The creatures make the surrounding forest trails hazardous for both Alliance sentinels and passing travelers. While yetis are common to the untamed reaches of Kalimdor, the denizens of Rage Scar Hold stand out for their raw aggression and territorial ferocity. Deeper in the dark corridors of the cave lie subtle clues of an older occupancy. Carved stonework and night elven architecture suggest the cavern was once a barrow den or an arcane sanctuary. Forgotten tomes and mystic markings remain among the dirt and bone, leaving travelers to wonder whether unfortunate scholars were slaughtered by the beasts or if the yetis somehow gravitate toward the lingering magic of the site.

subzone:raptor-ridge.text: Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge is an elevated, rugged expanse in the eastern Wetlands, sitting northwest of the fortified Dragonmaw Gates. It serves as the primary hunting and nesting grounds for packs of ferocious Razormaw raptors, overseen by a particularly vicious matriarch deep within its caverns. Rising above the sodden marshes of the eastern Wetlands, Raptor Ridge is among the most perilous wilderness areas in the region. Vicious Razormaw raptors prowl its crags and rocky trails in large packs, making travel near the foothills of Khaz Modan hazardous for wanderers. At the heart of the ridge lies a brooding cavern dominated by the Razormaw Matriarch, whose aggressive brood aggressively defends their nests against any encroaching predators or foolish travelers wandering too close to the Dragonmaw Gates.

subzone:ravencrest-monument.text: Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea. Scholars often speculate that the monument commemorates Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest, the famed noble who rallied and led the night elven host during the War of the Ancients after the fall of Zin-Azshari. However, its close proximity to the pre-Sundering city of Eldarath and ambiguous surviving stonework leave its true origins debated. Rather than pilgrims or night elven caretakers, the surrounding cliff is currently claimed by the serpentine Spitelash naga, who defend the fallen monument with vicious territorial aggression.

subzone:rebel-camp.text: Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades. Perched precariously near the Duskwood border, the Rebel Camp operates under constant threat. Cut off from regular Stormwind relief, Doren relies on covert supplies and defensive armaments—including goblin explosives brokered through Booty Bay—to hold the perimeter against Kurzen's raiding parties. For Alliance travelers venturing south into the savage jungle, the encampment provides a vital first foothold of sanity.

subzone:refuge-pointe.text: Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe is the primary redoubt for the Alliance and the surviving remnants of Stromgarde within the Arathi Highlands. Perched centrally along the highlands' trade road, it serves as a staging ground to reclaim the shattered capital of Stromgarde Keep and hold back rival forces across the region. Following the devastation of the Third War and the catastrophic fall of Stromgarde Keep, the bulk of Stromgarde's surviving populace fled south toward friendlier lands. Those who remained formed a resolute vanguard, digging in at Refuge Pointe under Captain Nials. Composed of battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers, League of Arathor forces, and supporting Alliance specialists, the encampment represents the kingdom's last organized stand in its ancestral homeland. Refuge Pointe is constantly on the brink of being overwhelmed. Hemmed in by the Forsaken and the Horde based out of Hammerfall, Witherbark trolls, Syndicate rogues, and Boulderfist ogres, the garrison has zero reserves to spare. When dwarven commanders at the battered Thandol Span desperately requested reinforcements to fight off the Dark Iron clan, Captain Nials had to refuse. Every sword, shield, and scrap of supply stationed at Refuge Pointe must remain dedicated to defending the highlands and preparing a counteroffensive to retake Stromgarde Keep.

subzone:roguefeather-den.text: Roguefeather Den. Roguefeather Den is a cavern nestled in the south-central reaches of Thousand Needles. Infested with ferocious screeching harpies, the cave serves as a fortified roost where the flock hoards scavenged provisions deep within its shadowed recesses. Carved into the sheer sandstone bluffs of southern Thousand Needles, Roguefeather Den is the foul nesting ground of local harpies. Known for their feral screeching and aggressive territorialism, the harpies treat the cavern as both a secure haven and a storehouse, vigilantly guarding the gathered food and stolen supplies they pile in the dark recesses at the back of the cave.

subzone:ruined-reaches.text: Ruined Reaches. The Ruined Reaches comprise the treacherous southern coastline of Azshara near the border with Durotar. Marked by crumbling ancient ruins, shattered shipwrecks, and jagged shallows, these beaches are overrun by aggressive shoreline predators. Amid the desolation, a small gnomish outpost perches high on a cliffside above the surf. Stretching along the southern borders of Azshara just north of Durotar, the Ruined Reaches are a maze of rocky inlets, cliff faces, and debris-strewn sand. Like the Jagged Reef further north, hidden shallows make maritime travel extremely hazardous, leaving numerous ruined vessels broken along the shore. The waters and beaches teem with hostile wildlife, including territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura, making overland transit just as dangerous as navigating the surf. Perched upon a western cliff overlooking the beaches sits an unexpected pocket of tinker civilization: a gnomish workshop accessible via a steep trail from Azshara's mainland. Run by Blimo and Jubie Gadgetspring, this outpost offers engineering components and general trade goods to passing adventurers. The interior features an elevator ascending to private quarters with three beds, though who—if anyone—claims the third bunk remains a quiet domestic mystery.

subzone:ruins-of-aboraz.text: Ruins of Aboraz. The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient Gurubashi stone ruins nestled along the southeastern cliffs of Stranglethorn Vale. Once part of the sprawling jungle troll empire, the crumbling terraces now serve as the secluded redoubt for the renegade witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls. Perched on the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine, the weathered masonry of Aboraz has been transformed into an alchemical testing ground. Zanzil the Outcast was banished by the local tribes and the mainlanders alike, retreating here to brew potent mind-altering concoctions and toxic elixirs. Within the stone courtyards, Zanzil exerts total control over an unsettling menagerie of servitors, including shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and even co-opted coastal naga.

subzone:ruins-of-alterac.text: Ruins of Alterac. The snow-covered Ruins of Alterac are all that remain of Alterac City, once the proud mountain capital of the Kingdom of Alterac. Cast out of the Alliance and put under martial law after King Aiden Perenolde's treason during the Second War, the shattered stronghold is now overrun by the brutish Crushridge ogres. Alterac was once an independent human realm carved out of the old Arathor empire, perched high on the trade routes through the mountains. During the Second War, fearing destruction at the hands of the invading Old Horde, King Aiden Perenolde secretly struck a pact with the orcs. When the betrayal was uncovered following the fighting at Caer Darrow, the Alliance of Lordaeron retaliated swiftly. King Terenas Menethil II put the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair as the populace fled or turned to outlawry. While surviving Alteraci nobles and rogue soldiers formed the Syndicate to wage guerrilla campaigns from towns like Strahnbrad, they lost their ancestral capital entirely. Today, the Crushridge ogres under Mug'thol dwell among the broken ramparts, palace halls, and wrecked ballistae. Neither the Syndicate nor the human defenders of Southshore have managed to reclaim the fallen city, leaving its crumbling towers and abandoned vaults as dangerous territory for treasure hunters and scavengers.

subzone:ruins-of-isildien.text: Ruins of Isildien. The Ruins of Isildien are the sprawling remains of an ancient night elven city in southwestern Feralas, destroyed ten millennia ago during the Great Sundering. Today, the overgrown stonework and cracked temple courtyards are occupied by brutish Gordunni ogres. Ten thousand years ago, before the world shattered, Isildien was a grand night elven settlement nestled in the primordial forests of ancient Kalimdor. Its graceful marble arches and grand terraces stood as monuments to kaldorei civilization and devotion. When the Well of Eternity imploded and tore the continents apart, Isildien fell into ruined desolation, smothered under millennia of untamed jungle growth.
