Dominating the upper terrace is a colossal domed structure remarkably reminiscent of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, suggesting the city was once a significant sanctuary dedicated to Elune. In the modern era, the elegant stonework of Isildien serves a far cruder purpose. The Gordunni ogres of Feralas have claimed the sprawling terraces and outcroppings as one of their primary settlements. The ogres have fortified the crumbling walkways, desecrating ancient plazas with crude bonfires, primitive barricades, and war banners, fiercely defending their stolen home against any outsiders who venture too close to the southern hills.

subzone:ruins-of-jubuwal.text: Ruins of Jubuwal. The Ruins of Jubuwal are the crumbling remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement located just east of the Gurubashi Arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Once a place of empire and ritual, the ruins have fallen under the sway of the rogue witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his bizarre retinue of minions. Situated off the primary thoroughfare cutting through Stranglethorn Vale, Jubuwal was once part of the grand Gurubashi civilization. Today, stone carvings and ivy-draped masonry have been overtaken by Zanzil the Outcast, an eccentric witch doctor known for his potent concoctions and foul voodoo. Zanzil has filled the ruins with an unnatural menagerie of followers, including enthralled ghouls, subjugated naga, and renegade trolls. Desperate fugitives also lurk among the stone arches, such as Jon-Jon the Crow and Maury 'Club Foot' Wilkins, both hiding from the ruthless debt collector 'Sea Wolf' MacKinley back in Booty Bay.

subzone:ruins-of-ravenwind.text: Ruins of Ravenwind. The Ruins of Ravenwind are the shattered remnants of an ancient Highborne city nestled in northern Feralas. Today, the crumbling marble structures are heavily infested by the vicious Northspring harpies and guarded by brooding dragonkin. Much like the great city of Dire Maul to the east, the Ruins of Ravenwind stand as a solemn monument to the height and hubris of ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering. Long abandoned by its original kaldorei architects, the site has succumbed to creeping wild foliage, forgotten arcane altars, and the foul roosts of Northspring harpies who prey on anything wandering beneath the shattered arches. Beyond the screeching harpies, Ravenwind is bordered by diverse and territorial threats. Fierce green dragonkin known as the Jaedemir circle the central groves and waterways, guarding ancient arboreal sites. Meanwhile, stray wanderers—from distracted night elf explorers to peculiar, solitary gnolls lingering nearby—frequently find themselves trapped in the crossfire of the ruins' lingering magics and wild predators.

subzone:ruins-of-zul-mamwe.text: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe. Tucked away in a mountainous pocket south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe serve as a heavily fortified stronghold for the Skullsplitter troll tribe. Enclosed by steep cliffs on almost all sides, the ancient stone platforms now teem with fierce jungle trolls under the rule of their ruthless chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel. The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe represent one of the primary seats of power for the Skullsplitter tribe in central Stranglethorn Vale. Cradled within a natural mountain amphitheater, the site has only a single open approach from the north, making it an exceptional defensive redoubt. From atop its weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors, defending their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and rival jungle troll tribes. Like many of the stone settlements dotting the jungle, Zul'Mamwe is a relic of the ancient Gurubashi Empire that once held undisputed dominion over the southern reaches of the continent. Although the grand empire splintered long ago into squabbling, hostile factions, modern Skullsplitters fiercely guard these ancestral stones, continuing age-old tribal rituals amid the overgrown masonry and broken monoliths.

subzone:rustmaul-dig-site.text: Rustmaul Dig Site. The Rustmaul Dig Site is a ruined excavation in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats. Originally established by the dwarven Explorers' League to unearth ancient ruins, the camp fell into tragedy when a Horde war party slaughtered the miners, after which a subterranean silithid swarm emerged. Now abandoned by mortals, the site crawls with hostile insectoids emerging from the caverns below. Prospectors from the Ironforge Explorers' League set up the Rustmaul Dig Site hoping to uncover forgotten artifacts buried beneath the salt flats. Their efforts were brutally cut short when an aggressive Horde war party, led by Moktar Krin, fell upon the camp and wiped out the dwarven excavators. However, the conquerors enjoyed no triumph. The violent clash apparently disturbed a dormant cave network beneath the site, releasing an endless horde of silithid insects that quickly overwhelmed and drove off the battered survivors. Today, Rustmaul stands entirely lost to the surface races. What remains of the mining equipment and scaffolds is buried under skittering mandibles and alien carapaces. The surviving members of Moktar Krin's war party retreated north to Ironstone Camp, terrified by the unrelenting tide of insectoids that emerged after their attack.

subzone:saltspray-glen.text: Saltspray Glen. Saltspray Glen is a windswept expanse in the northwestern Wetlands hugging the shores of Baradin Bay. Strong coastal gales regularly fling briny seawater across the mossy lowland, which is overrun by aggressive wild raptors. It forms a treacherous natural corridor between neighboring murloc-infested marshes and ancient dwarven ruins. Tucked away in the far northwestern reach of the Wetlands, Saltspray Glen takes its name from the sea spray driven inland off Baradin Bay whenever coastal gales kick up. Bordered by the murloc-haunted waters of Bluegill Marsh to the south and the quiet bluffs of Ironbeard's Tomb to the east, the glen offers little comfort to passing travelers. Packs of cunning wild raptors nest throughout the marshy grass, hunting along the brackish flats alongside their kin from nearby Raptor Ridge and Black Channel Marsh.

subzone:salty-sailor-tavern.text: Salty Sailor Tavern. The Salty Sailor Tavern is the beating heart of Booty Bay's social life, serving as the port's primary inn and watering hole. Run by the goblin Innkeeper Skindle, it welcomes scoundrels, mercenaries, and travelers from both factions seeking respite from the perils of the jungle. Perched amidst the wooden tiers of Booty Bay, the Salty Sailor Tavern offers warm beds and strong drinks under the watchful eye of the Blackwater Raiders. Behind the bar stands Innkeeper Skindle, keeping glasses filled while a menagerie of buccaneers, traders, and adventurers mingle on neutral ground. Outside the establishment hangs a massive, curious curio—a Zul'Gurub Protector Stone—serving as a strange trophy in this bustling den of commerce.

subzone:sanctum-stromgarde-keep.text: Sanctum (Stromgarde Keep). The Sanctum is a sacred redoubt tucked behind the chapel within Stromgarde Keep. Sheltered within the crumbling fortress, it guards the entrance to the ancestral Trollbane family crypt and stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst Arathi's ruin. While much of Stromgarde Keep has fallen to Syndicate infiltrators and the Boulderfist ogres, the Sanctum and its adjacent chapel have remained under the fierce protection of the surviving Stromgarde defenders. Located behind the house of worship, the Sanctum borders the citadel's graveyard and marks the threshold to the royal crypt where the kings of Stromgarde rest. For the battered loyalists rallying around Prince Galen Trollbane, holding this hallowed ground represents more than a tactical foothold; it is a desperate fight to keep their kingdom's ancestral heritage and faith from being trampled by invaders. Beneath the stone flags of the Sanctum lies the passage into the royal tomb. The ground here is consecrated, intended as a place of peaceful reflection and worship of the Holy Light. In the wake of King Thoras Trollbane's murder and the kingdom's subsequent collapse, the Sanctum has instead become a defensive retreat. Those seeking to breach the inner sanctum must contend not only with the royal guards garrisoned throughout the halls, but with the haunting reality of an ancient human lineage clinging to survival on its sacred threshold.

subzone:sar-theris-strand.text: Sar'theris Strand. Sar'theris Strand forms the western coastline of Desolace, fronting the Veiled Sea. In stark contrast to the barren, grey inland wastes, the shore is sunny and grassy, though it remains perilous due to prowling naga, sea giants, and makrura. Running the length of western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand offers a bizarre respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Here, the clifftops and beaches are bright and green. Yet the strand is far from welcoming: serpentine naga patrol the surf alongside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Shipwrecks litter the shoals, including the ruined Karnitol vessel to the north and small shattered skiffs beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor, proving the sea is as treacherous as the shore. Beyond the constant threat of naga and giants, the waters off the strand are known among seasoned travelers for their peculiar bounties. The jagged coastal shallows conceal salvage from lost expeditions and merchant ventures, while the deep surf is home to rare marine wildlife, notably the prized Sar'theris Striker fish sought out by master fishermen across Kalimdor.

subzone:sardor-isle.text: Sardor Isle. Sardor Isle is a lush island situated off the western coast of Feralas, north of the perilous Isle of Dread. It serves as the home to Feathermoon Stronghold, the primary night elven military bastion in southern Kalimdor. Despite the heavy sentinel presence, parts of the island remain prowled by wild beasts and hostile naga creeping up from the shallows. Resting across the water from mainland Feralas, Sardor Isle is anchored by Feathermoon Stronghold, an impressive elven garrison commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon. While the fortress itself is heavily fortified and linked to the mainland via regular ferry crossings, the broader island is far from tame. Roaming wolf packs claim the timbered slopes, while encroaching naga lurk along the rocky western and northern beaches, constantly testing the resolve of the night elven sentinels.

subzone:sargeron.text: Sargeron. Sargeron is the crumbled ruin of an ancient night elf city located in northern Desolace. Shattered during the Great Sundering, its former temples of Elune have been defiled and claimed by the Hatefury satyrs, who renamed the grounds in tribute to their master, Sargeras. Before the War of the Ancients broke the continent, this settlement was a flourishing center of worship dedicated to Elune, housing sacred grounds such as Elune's Temple, Sanctuary, and Cathedral. Its true name is lost to antiquity. When the world shattered, the city collapsed into rubble, leaving behind sanctified relics like the Cup of Elune, Elune's Brazier, and Elune's Handmaiden. In the millennia since, corrupted Hatefury satyrs overran the stones, repurposing the sacred Kaldorei architecture into a stronghold honoring the titan Sargeras.

subzone:savage-coast.text: Savage Coast. The Savage Coast is the rugged western shoreline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the southern border of Westfall down toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Prowled by river crocolisks, shore basilisks, and hostile troll tribes, the strand earns its brutal name with every tide. Running from the cliffs bordering Westfall south toward Grom'gol Base Camp, the Savage Coast marks the perilous western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. The sandy banks offer little hospitality: snapjaws, crocolisks, and stonestalkers roam freely among the tide pools and drift logs. Just inland lie territorial jungle troll encampments, making any casual walk along the beach a fight for survival. Offshore, the waters dip toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef, ensuring that danger lurks both on the sand and under the waves.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-armory.text: Scarlet Monastery Armory. The Armory is the fortified martial wing of the Scarlet Monastery, dedicated to manufacturing weapons and training recruits for the Scarlet Crusade. Behind locked iron gates, ranks of zealous footmen and crusaders drill under the fierce command of Herod, the Scarlet Champion. Once part of a peaceful retreat for Lordaeron's priesthood, the monastery was completely overhauled following the Third War. The Armory now serves as the Crusade's primary forge, weapons depot, and combat proving ground. From the open training grounds to the deep weapon halls, ranks of Scarlet footmen, conjurers, and crusaders prepare relentlessly to purge the Scourge and anyone else they deem tainted. The wing remains locked away from the Grand Vestibule, accessible only to those carrying the Scarlet Key found in the neighboring Library. At the heart of the wing lies the Hall of Champions, lined with towering statues dedicated to legendary heroes of the Crusade's past. The hall is overseen by Herod, a brutal warrior whose ferocity and whirlwinds are legendary among the crusaders. Herod trains the next generation of zealots personally; when hard-pressed in battle, his desperate recruits will pour into the chamber to fight and die for their champion.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-cathedral.text: Scarlet Monastery Cathedral. The Cathedral is the spiritual and military heart of the Scarlet Monastery, housing the Crusade's inner sanctum. Once a serene hall of worship for Lordaeron's priesthood, it now serves as the command seat for High Inquisitor Whitemane and Scarlet Commander Mograine, guarded by the Crusade's most devoted zealots. Once a peaceful center of enlightenment and prayer for the priesthood of Lordaeron, the Cathedral fell into madness in the wake of the Third War. Following the fall of the kingdom to the Scourge, surviving zealots transformed the complex into a fortress of unyielding hatred. Beyond the manicured cloister of the Chapel Gardens lies the grand Crusader's Chapel, where priests and warriors gather in devotion to their crusade. They view all outsiders—regardless of race or faction—as carriers of the undead plague who must be cleansed by blade and holy fire.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-library.text: Scarlet Monastery Library. The Library is the eastern wing of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades, once dedicated to holy scholarship and Lordaeron's priesthood. Now guarded by battle hounds and zealots, it houses ancient archives and rare tomes fiercely coveted by scholars and mages from both factions. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a center for learning and enlightenment for Lordaeron's priesthood. The eastern cloisters housed vast archives of religious thought, historical records, and arcane treatises. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the Scourge, they retained these repositories, turning the quiet halls into an armed redoubt. Today, beastmasters run tracking hounds through the courtyards while battle-mages patrol the shelves, guarding historic volumes like the Compendium of the Fallen and ancient research on the Titans against outsiders. Breaching the Library requires navigating past Houndmaster Loksey in the Huntsman's Cloister, whose trained hounds sniff out infiltrators seeking passage into the inner chambers. Beyond the Gallery of Treasures lies the Athenaeum, overseen by Arcanist Doan. A formidable mage who wields devastating fire and protective sorcery, Doan studies in isolation, fiercely defending the Crusade's hoarded knowledge from any who venture into the heart of the complex.

subzone:shadow-hold.text: Shadow Hold. Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor. Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

subzone:shadowbreak-ravine.text: Shadowbreak Ravine. Shadowbreak Ravine is a secluded mountain hollow tucked away in southeastern Desolace. Cloaked among jagged crags near Magram Village, this eerie ravine serves as a hidden redoubt for the demonic forces and mortal zealots of the Burning Blade. Tucked deep into the barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine provides the Burning Blade with a secluded staging ground away from the eyes of wandering centaur tribes. Amid strange, oversized mushrooms and grim ritual encampments, cultists labor alongside summoned demons. Here, dark practitioners invoke fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains, using the natural isolation of the ravine to marshal reinforcements and maintain a firm demonic foothold within the badlands of Desolace.

subzone:shady-rest-inn.text: Shady Rest Inn. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Today, only charred timbers and smoldering ashes remain following a sudden and violent arson attack. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues. Built to serve travelers navigating the treacherous crossing between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, the Shady Rest Inn stood as an outpost of civilized comfort in a harsh wilderness. That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.

subzone:shaper-s-terrace.text: Shaper's Terrace. Perched high on the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, the Shaper's Terrace is a mysterious overlook marked by ancient titan architecture. It is named in honor of Khaz'goroth the Shaper and bears quiet witness to the primordial experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. Overlooking the lush, prehistoric basin of Un'Goro Crater, the Shaper's Terrace holds monumental stone edifices left behind by the titans. Believed to be dedicated to Khaz'goroth the Shaper, this high plateau stands as a testament to the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth. From these elevated stones, ancient entities once observed and directed the flora and fauna below. Its cold stone arches and massive metallic plinths stand in stark, enigmatic contrast to the untamed wilderness thriving directly beneath them.

subzone:shattered-strand.text: Shattered Strand. The Shattered Strand is a wild, rugged coastline flanking the northern rim of the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Dominated by crashing surf and crumbling ancient ruins, the beach crawls with hazardous marine beasts and tribal aquatic creatures. Stretching along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms, the Shattered Strand is far from a peaceful shoreline. The rocky beaches and tidal shallows are heavily inhabited by aggressive wildlife, including towering sea giants, multi-headed hydras, and snapping makrura, alongside encampments of coastal murlocs. Crumbling elven architecture overlooks the waves, anchored by landmarks such as the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the solitary Tower of Eldara. For travelers navigating Azshara's treacherous cliffs, descending to this isolated strip of coast means confronting some of the region's deadliest amphibious threats.

subzone:shifting-mire.text: Shifting Mire. The Shifting Mire forms the vast, muddy heart of the Swamp of Sorrows, lying just west of the Pool of Tears. Its name comes from the strange, restless silt beneath the murky water, which seems to drift and gather under the influence of an unseen force. Spanning the central reaches of the marshland, the Shifting Mire is an unsettling expanse where solid footing is hard to come by. The silt along the swamp floor shifts and collects as though moved by a living will, driven by a strange, ambient energy permeating the peat. Amidst the drifting mud prowl predatory swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks, while bands of broken draenei known as the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

subzone:slag-pit.text: Slag Pit. The Slag Pit is an extensive subterranean mining excavation nestled inside the Cauldron of Searing Gorge. Overseen by ruthless Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers, these fiery tunnels are driven by forced labor under the shadow of Blackrock Mountain. Trespassers must contend not only with hostile dwarf overseers, but also ravenous incendosaurs prowling the lower levels. Carved into the depths of the Cauldron, the Slag Pit represents the grinding industrial engine of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge. Day and night, enslaved workers are driven to extract rich ores and minerals under the lash of brutal overseers and taskmasters. The environment is harsh and suffocating, dominated by scorching heat, choking dust, and the clatter of iron picks. The Dark Irons maintain ruthless discipline over their excavation, violently repelling any outside interference with their supply lines to Blackrock Depths. Beyond the cruelty of the slavers, the physical tunnels themselves pose a deadly hazard to workers and intruders alike. In the lower reaches of the excavation, the earth breaks open into scorching caverns inhabited by incendosaurs—ferocious reptilian beasts native to the fiery underground. Despite the constant danger of being devoured by these subterranean predators, the Dark Iron masters continue to push their labor force deeper into the rock, entirely indifferent to the lives lost in the process.

subzone:slaughter-hollow.text: Slaughter Hollow. Slaughter Hollow is a secluded ogre mound tucked away in the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains. Controlled by the brutish Crushridge clan, it stands as a rough camp rather than a bustling settlement. Travelers rarely have reason to trespass unless hunting ogres or exploring the frozen mountain passes. Hidden high in the peaks bordering Hillsbrad and Alterac, Slaughter Hollow serves as an encampment for the local Crushridge ogres. Like many ogre mounds scattered across the highlands, it is littered with makeshift bonfires, discarded bones, and crude shelters. While other ogre dens in the mountains see frequent conflicts over territory or stolen supplies, Slaughter Hollow remains largely quiet and bypassed by major military campaigns. Due to its seclusion, the mound occasionally serves as a holding place for unlucky prisoners taken along the mountain trails. Word among travelers tells of an unfortunate gnome named Rizz Loosebolt who has found himself locked in a crude cage here, attempting to barter with anyone passing by. Such unfortunate captives rarely fare well against the appetite of the Crushridge clan.

subzone:slithering-scar.text: Slithering Scar. The Slithering Scar is a sprawling silithid hive dominating the southern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Home to the aggressive Gorishi swarm, its excavated tunnels and organic spires represent a dangerous insectoid encroachment into the primeval basin. Gouged into the red earth and rock of southern Un'Goro, the Slithering Scar stands as an alien intrusion against the lush prehistoric landscape. The hive is controlled by the Gorishi silithid, an organized strain of insectoids that have honeycombed the cliffs with damp burrows and egg chambers. Within these subterranean warrens, workers and tunnelers nurture vast clutches of eggs and grubs alongside towering wasp broods. More alarmingly, the colony cultivates fledgling silithid colossi, monstrous behemoths intended to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystalline formations nestled within the hive pulse with unnatural resonance, acting as focal points for the colony's dark, coordinated will. Scholars and explorers who traverse the perimeter of Un'Goro often notice a disturbing anomaly regarding the hive's location. While ancient crystalline pylons stand sentinel across the northern, eastern, and western boundaries of the basin, the southern reaches possess no such pillar. It is precisely in this unprotected gap that the Gorishi have burrowed inward from the neighboring deserts. Whether the silithid purposefully undermined a forgotten southern ward or simply invaded where the crater's primordial wards were weakest remains an unsettling mystery to those watching their rapid expansion.

subzone:sorrowmurk.text: Sorrowmurk. The Sorrowmurk is the treacherous wetland expanse lying directly east of the Pool of Tears in the Swamp of Sorrows. Long dominated by patrolling green dragonkin guarding the approach to the Sunken Temple, it remains one of the most perilous regions in the eastern marshes. Stretching out along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, the Sorrowmurk is a dense and murky mire that borders the Forbidding Sea. For years, the waters and tangled boughs have crawled with ferocious green dragonspawn and towering drakes, remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence ensures that only seasoned travelers dare wander through its sodden reaches.

subzone:southern-savage-coast.text: Southern Savage Coast. The Southern Savage Coast encompasses the long strand of beaches and tidal waters hugging southwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Flanked by the treacherous depths of the South Seas, these shores are home to prowling wildlife, hostile naga, and the ever-present threat of coastal raiders. Stretching down the western edge of the southern jungle, the Southern Savage Coast marks where the mainland gives way to the warm currents of the South Seas. Divided from the northern Savage Coast by the submerged ruins and perils of the Vile Reef, this coastline skirts inlets near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring before tapering off past Booty Bay and Janeiro's Point. While the beaches offer open ground compared to the suffocating interior jungle, travelers must contend with aggressive reptilian predators, predatory naga hunting the shallows, and passing corsairs scanning the strand for easy prey.

subzone:southfury-river.text: Southfury River. The Southfury River is one of the most prominent waterways on central Kalimdor, carving a swift and wide path southward from the heights of Mount Hyjal. It forms the natural border separating Azshara from Ashenvale, as well as Durotar from the Barrens, before plunging into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Beginning high in Mount Hyjal, the Southfury drops over dramatic cascades before coursing through central Kalimdor. Its roaring waters serve as a clear geographic divide, separating the sacred forests of Ashenvale from ancient Azshara, and dividing the arid hills of Durotar from the savanna of the Barrens. Only a few strategic bridges dare cross its swift currents—most notably the heavy span guarding the rear gates of Orgrimmar and the crossing connecting Durotar to the Barrens. The river eventually empties into the Great Sea via a cascading waterfall just northeast of the neutral port of Ratchet. For the Horde, the Southfury is both a shield and a vital natural highway. It protects the western approaches of Durotar and Orgrimmar from immediate ground assault while supplying fresh mountain runoff through an otherwise scorched, sun-baked landscape. Just north of the western crossing into Orgrimmar lies a singular geographic crossroads where four major territories converge: Ashenvale, Azshara, Durotar, and the Barrens. Control over this churning waterway ensures supply lines between Orgrimmar and the outlying Horde settlements remain intact.

subzone:southmoon-ruins.text: Southmoon Ruins. The Southmoon Ruins are ancient stone remains situated in southern Tanaris, just north of the Valley of the Watchers. Long claimed by the brutish Dunemaul ogres, the crumbling stonework preserves remnants of the ancient troll civilization that dominated the desert before the sands swallowed it. Rising out of the blistering wastes of southern Tanaris, the Southmoon Ruins stand as a weathered testament to the ancient troll empires that once ruled Kalimdor's southern reaches. Like nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade, its stone pillars and altars have weathered thousands of years of wind and abrasive grit. The site has often served as a squalid camp for the Dunemaul ogres, who show little reverence for the craftsmanship of the past, using the ancient structures purely for shelter and territory. The architectural remnants are unmistakably trollish, but little is recorded of the people who raised Southmoon's stones or why they abandoned them. Whatever they left behind lies buried beneath the drifting sand, and the ogres who squat among the pillars care nothing for it.

subzone:southpoint-tower.text: Southpoint Tower. Southpoint Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated at the western border of Hillsbrad Foothills, overlooking the road to Silverpine Forest. Once a human sentry post, the shattered structure is now utilized by Forsaken scouts keeping watch over Alliance movements in the region. Standing just south of the highway linking Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills, Southpoint Tower was originally built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard traffic moving between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. Following the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Today, it stands roofless and crumbling, an isolated relic of human dominion in a fractured territory. Despite its collapsed state, the vantage point remains tactically valuable. The Forsaken maintain an outpost here, stationing agents such as Deathstalker Lesh to spy on local Alliance patrols, the nearby human settlements of Hillsbrad Fields, and travelers passing along the primary road. Because of its lonely location right near hostile territory, the tower frequently becomes a flashpoint for skirmishes.

subzone:southshore-town-hall.text: Southshore Town Hall. Southshore Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the southern coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, standing as one of the last functioning centers of Lordaeron's civil authority. From inside, Magistrate Henry Maleb coordinates local defenses and governs the town's surviving populace. The hall is a vital hub for the Alliance as they struggle to maintain a foothold in the plagued north. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered under Scourge corruption and Forsaken expansion, Southshore's town hall maintains the semblance of an intact human government. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees daily governance from his office here, working alongside officials like Kundric Zanden to secure resources and preserve civic order. In a region surrounded by aggressive undead, Syndicate rogues, and Hillsbrad's fierce border skirmishes, the hall is the nerve center directing the town's survival against constant threats.

subzone:stagalbog.text: Stagalbog. The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness. Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here. Because it borders the Pool of Tears, the Stagalbog frequently catches whatever shadows or corruptions seep from the Sunken Temple.

subzone:stagalbog-cave.text: Stagalbog Cave. Stagalbog Cave is a damp subterranean cavern situated in the Stagalbog within the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as a fortified den for the Marsh murlocs and their sinister spiritual leader, the Swamp Talker. Tucked away in the murky eastern wetlands of the Swamp of Sorrows, Stagalbog Cave provides shelter from the relentless swamp rains for the local murlocs. Known as the Marsh tribe, these amphibious creatures aggressively guard the winding cavern chambers alongside their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Travelers venturing near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog often hear their gurgling calls echoing out across the mossy banks, warning trespassers away from their nesting grounds.

subzone:stonard.text: Stonard. Stonard is a fortified Horde outpost situated in the southern marshes of the Swamp of Sorrows. Originally built during the First War, it serves the modern Horde as an essential foothold in the southern Eastern Kingdoms and an observation post watching the Blasted Lands. Stonard stands as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth. First established when the Old Horde spilled through the Dark Portal into what was once the Black Morass, Stonard and its sister post, Rockard, anchored the invaders' lines. Though abandoned and damaged during the fallout of the Second War, Thrall's New Horde moved to reconstruct and garrison Stonard. Anchored by a traditional orcish Great Hall and fortified burrows, the outpost is now a vital island of Horde authority in an untamed, perilous mire. Modern Stonard functions as both an expeditionary camp and a staging ground. Cartographers and scouts fan out across the surrounding muck to map the uncharted swamp and monitor hostile native beasts, lost draenei wanderers, and the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar to the east. Crucially, Stonard also provides the Horde with an organized staging post just north of the shattered Blasted Lands, ensuring a watchful eye remains near the dormant Dark Portal.

subzone:stonemaul-ruins.text: Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul Ruins are the shattered remnants of Stonemaul Village, once the proud Kalimdor settlement of the Stonemaul ogres. After being driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north, leaving their former home overrun by Firemane dragonspawn. Following their migration to Kalimdor, the Stonemaul ogres founded their settlement amid the murky swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. The village became famous when the beastmaster Rexxar braved the clan's lethal trials, slew their brutal chieftain Kor'gall, and rallied the ogres to defend the nascent Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces. After the war, Rexxar left the ogre Mok'Morokk in command. Under Mok'Morokk's selfish rule, the village fell into decline and was ultimately ambushed and shattered by the black dragonflight. The surviving ogres fled north to establish Brackenwall Village, while Onyxia's brood took complete possession of the ruins. Today, the ruins are firmly ensconced within Dragonmurk and crawl with Firemane dragonspawn tending the brood's nearby nesting grounds. While Overlord Mok'Morokk grew cowardly and content to languish in Brackenwall, older and prouder clan members like Tharg and Draz'Zilb refuse to abandon their homeland. Operating out of Brackenwall, they urge Horde champions to slaughter the occupying dragonspawn and smash the dragonflight's eggs in hopes that the Stonemaul may one day march back and reclaim their ancestral village.

subzone:stonewrought-pass.text: Stonewrought Pass. Stonewrought Pass is an underground tunnel cut directly through the southern mountains of Loch Modan into the blighted expanse of the Searing Gorge. Masterfully engineered by the famed architect Franclorn Forgewright, this passage connects the Valley of Kings directly to Dustfire Valley. Heavy iron gates secure both ends to protect peaceful dwarven lands from the volcanic terrors to the south. Carved out of the bedrock by the legendary master architect Franclorn Forgewright—famed also for the massive Stonewrought Dam—the Stonewrought Pass serves as a direct corridor between the pastoral beauty of Loch Modan and the scorched wastes of Searing Gorge. Emerging in Loch Modan near the colossal Valley of Kings, it cuts straight through the mountain ridge down into Dustfire Valley. Because Searing Gorge is infested with Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts, the Ironforge mountaineers keep the passage locked tight behind heavy gates to prevent danger from spilling into the north.

subzone:stromgarde-keep.text: Stromgarde Keep. Stromgarde Keep is the battered, divided capital of the fallen human kingdom of Stromgarde in the Arathi Highlands. Once the proud cradle of human civilization known as Strom, the fortress is now partitioned between hostile Syndicate rogues, invading Boulderfist ogres, and a desperate remnant of royal defenders under Prince Galen Trollbane. Long before it bore its current name, this fortress was founded nearly three millennia ago as Strom, the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor under King Thoradin. It served as the staging ground for humanity's victory against the forest trolls and was the birthplace of human wizardry, where high elven magi tutored the first hundred human spellcasters. Over centuries, as younger sister kingdoms like Dalaran, Lordaeron, and Stormwind rose and prospered, Strom's influence waned. Renamed Stromgarde by the stubborn Trollbane dynasty who stayed behind, it remained a proud warrior bastion throughout the Second War, anchoring the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde. Following the devastation of the Third War, Stromgarde finally buckled under mounting catastrophes and treachery. Today, the majestic stone city sits fractured into three warring sectors. The aristocratic traitors of the Syndicate occupy the grand inner keep, while brutish Boulderfist ogres have overrun the former sanctum of the mage district. Pinned in the remaining quarter, Prince Galen Trollbane and the battered Stromgarde military wage a grueling, bloody war on multiple fronts just to keep their ancestral home from vanishing into memory.

subzone:sundown-marsh.text: Sundown Marsh. Sundown Marsh marks the deepest, westernmost reaches of the Wetlands where stagnant waters meet treacherous wildlife. Despite the prowling raptors, oozes, and gnolls, an eccentric pair maintains a solitary homestead along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh sits tucked into the northwest of the Wetlands, characterized by deep water, thick mud, and a dense population of predators. Giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls roam freely through the mist. The hazardous terrain keeps most passing travelers strictly to the main cobblestone road connecting Menethil Harbor to Ironforge, leaving this deep corner largely untamed. Amid the hazards of the marsh stands a lonely stone cottage topped with a churning windmill. There, the gnome Fradd Swiftgear and the dwarf Wenna Silkbeard make an unlikely living scavenging the bog. They peddle curiosities and rare trade recipes recovered from the mire to travelers brave enough to navigate the marsh's aggressive denizens.

subzone:sunnyglade.text: Sunnyglade. Sunnyglade was once a wealthy, prosperous human settlement belonging to the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War. Devastated and eventually abandoned as the front lines collapsed, the ruined settlement now languishes under the dark influence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the First War tore southern Azeroth apart, Sunnyglade was celebrated for its wealth and comfortable prosperity. That peace was violently shattered when the Old Horde invaded. Orc raiding parties attacked the town and enslaved its surviving residents, leaving only a lone wizard's tower intact to study the arcane arts of human conjurers. Though Stormwind forces mounted an effort to rescue the captive peasants and rebuild the settlement, the surrounding Riverglades were steadily swallowed by the advancing Horde. Deeming the outer province lost, Stormwind's commanders eventually withdrew their resources to defend the homeland, leaving Sunnyglade to ruin. Today, Sunnyglade lies far beyond the safe borders of Stormwind's reestablished realm. While the iconic stone mage tower remarkably weathered the First War and the years of abandonment that followed, the peaceful township around it is gone. Instead, the secluded ruins have been occupied by zealots of the Twilight's Hammer cult, who turn the once-prosperous valley to their own sinister designs.

subzone:swamplight-manor.text: Swamplight Manor. Swamplight Manor is an ironically named, ramshackle wooden shack nestled deep within Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the eccentric home and kitchen of 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, an isolated recluse known across the mire for his strange culinary appetites. Despite its humble, eerie isolation, the surrounding garden conceals intrigue that catches the attention of both Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Despite what its grandiose title suggests, Swamplight Manor is far from a lordly estate. It is merely a crooked, weather-beaten shack tucked into the haunted wetlands of Witch Hill. Its lone resident, the odd recluse known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, lives a solitary existence surrounded by fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts. Jarl spends his days concocting unusual regional delicacies out of local wildlife, frequently recruiting wandering adventurers to hunt down bizarre ingredients like marsh frog legs and creature eyes to satisfy his strange craft.

subzone:tabetha-s-farm.text: Tabetha's Farm. Deep in the murkiest reaches of the Quagmire lies Tabetha's Farm, an isolated homestead centered around a small wooden hut, a modest garden, and a private dock. Despite the treacherous marsh surroundings, this sanctuary serves as a hidden redoubt for the hermit mage Tabetha. Tucked away in the western wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Tabetha's Farm defies its unforgiving environment. Consisting of a weather-worn hut, small vegetable plots, and a dock for navigating the swamp's murky waterways, the homestead offers a quiet refuge far from the political rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Here, the reclusive human sorceress Tabetha lives in near-total seclusion, pursuing esoteric studies of arcane and fel power without interference from Dalaran or local authorities. Despite its remote location, the farm attracts practitioners of the magical arts from across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Mages seeking mastery over raw arcane surges and warlocks seeking aid to cleanse volatile artifacts like the Orb of Orahil are directed to Tabetha's doorstep.

subzone:tahonda-ruins.text: Tahonda Ruins. The Tahonda Ruins are the sun-bleached remnants of an ancient tauren settlement swallowed by the salt and sand of the Shimmering Flats. Little is remembered of the villagers who once lived here, and dangerous Saltstone basilisks now stalk among the decaying tent poles and shredded leather. Situated in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats near the pass into Tanaris, the Tahonda Ruins stand as a somber monument to an abandoned tauren past. The village fell long ago, its weathered structures gradually engulfed by shifting white salt crusts. While some suspect the local Saltstone basilisks drove the inhabitants away, odd clues linger on the surviving structures. Two distinct sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge, suggesting the village met a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders before the desert claimed what remained.

subzone:tainted-scar.text: Tainted Scar. The Tainted Scar is a demon-infested canyon carved into the southwestern Blasted Lands, saturated with foul fel magic from the nearby Dark Portal. It currently serves as the primary redoubt for the remnants of the Burning Legion on Azeroth, commanded by the doomguard Lord Kazzak. Once lush wetlands belonging to the ancient Black Morass, this desolate trench was utterly drained of life and turned the color of dried blood by chaotic fel energies leaking from the Dark Portal. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, surviving forces of the Burning Legion rallied in the south. The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Tainted Scar as his stronghold, stationing elite demons across its blackened rises and dispatching dreadful lieutenants like Razelikh the Defiler to hold dominion over the wasted red soils. While most mortals shun the Scar on pain of agonizing death, practitioners of the dark arts find its saturated fel energies irresistible. An eccentric human warlock named Daio the Decrepit has taken up residence by a ruined demonic altar overlooking the horrors, using the rampant fiends to perform dark rituals and instruct aspiring warlocks in how to summon and bind dread infernals.

subzone:talonbranch-glade.text: Talonbranch Glade. Talonbranch Glade is a quiet night elf redoubt nestled in the blighted hills of northern Felwood. Located just south of Timbermaw Hold, it provides a rare haven of pristine moonlight, sanctuary, and hippogryph transit in an otherwise corrupted wilderness. Perched on high ground near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold, Talonbranch Glade serves as the northernmost bastion of the Alliance in Felwood. Centered around a sheltered night elf lodge and a functioning moonwell, the outpost offers a crucial refuge from the demonic corruption that has swallowed the surrounding forest. Alliance scouts, Sentinels, and passing adventurers use the glade to rest, recover, and plan their excursions deeper into the tainted woods or onward toward Winterspring and Moonglade. Aside from its natural and spiritual defenses, Talonbranch Glade functions as an essential logistics hub. Hippogryphs stationed here connect travelers to Auberdine in Darkshore and Everlook in the snowy expanse beyond Timbermaw Hold. It remains a lonely, vigilant watchpost holding the line against the encroaching shadows of the Shadow Council and feral beast packs roaming the corrupted vales.

subzone:temple-of-arkkoran.text: Temple of Arkkoran. The Temple of Arkkoran is an ancient night elven ruin resting on the northeastern cliffs of Azshara above the Shattered Strand. Originally built in honor of Elune, the crumbling structure has since been claimed by the towering sea giant Arkkoroc and his aquatic thralls. Like many of the grand ruins dotting Azshara's coast, the Temple of Arkkoran was once a sanctum dedicated to the moon goddess Elune before the Sundering shattered the ancient night elf empire. Today, its weathered marble steps and broken colonnades are overrun by tidal monstrosities. The sea giant Arkkoroc presides over the temple's highest level, surrounded by loyal makrura and vicious murlocs who violently defend the surrounding coastline from any land-dwelling intruders.

subzone:temple-of-atal-hakkar.text: Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, widely known as the Sunken Temple, is a submerged fortress built by exiled troll priests dedicated to the blood god Hakkar. Sunk beneath the marshes by the green dragonflight centuries ago, its drowned halls remain a staging ground for forbidden rituals and dark corruption. Over a millennium ago, a catastrophic civil war shattered the Gurubashi Empire when the Atal'ai priesthood attempted to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer. Exiled to the north, the surviving zealots raised a massive stone temple in the Swamp of Sorrows to finish their dark work. Learning of their scheme, the Dragon Aspect Ysera smashed the ziggurat deep into the mire, inundating its chambers beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragon wardens were left behind to guard the drowned ruins and ensure Hakkar's return was thwarted forever. Instead of burying the cult, the temple's submersion provided the Atal'ai isolation to continue their grisly sacrifices unhindered. Over the centuries, corruption began to rot the guardians from within; the dragon sentinels succumb to madness while the Atal'ai, guided by Jammal'an the Prophet, prepare the way for Hakkar's avatar. Now, both the Horde and Alliance keep an anxious eye on the submerged ziggurat as shadowy rumors slip out from the swamp's depths.

subzone:temple-of-zin-malor.text: Temple of Zin-Malor. The Temple of Zin-Malor is an ancient night elven sanctuary located within the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Originally dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, the crumbling structure is now held by the Spitelash naga under the direct command of Warlord Krellian. Before the Great Sundering, the Temple of Zin-Malor stood as a grand house of worship dedicated to Elune. Its architecture closely mirrors both the nearby Temple of Arkkoran and the modern Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, bearing the graceful, sweeping stonework characteristic of pre-Sundering night elven civilization. Today, however, its moonlit marble is weathered and broken, overtaken by the serpent-bodied Spitelash naga. These invaders have claimed the holy grounds for themselves, turning a place of quiet reflection into a militarized redoubt. The temple once housed the renowned Crystal of Zin-Malor, a potent artifact that was carried away long ago to Kel'Theril in Winterspring.

subzone:terrace-of-repose.text: Terrace of Repose. The Terrace of Repose is a pristine courtyard garden located just outside the entrance to the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Maintained by the Scarlet Crusade, it stands as one of the few places in northern Lordaeron completely untouched by the Plague of Undeath, complete with green hedges and clean water. Situated just north of the grand entrance into the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose offers a surreal contrast to the rotting forests of Tirisfal Glades. While the rest of Lordaeron chokes under grey mist, corrupt soil, and stagnant bogs, this terrace boasts verdant, neatly pruned hedges and a functioning fountain fed by fresh, uncontaminated water. For the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, the garden serves as physical proof of their divine righteousness and purity, a sacred bastion demonstrating that holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

subzone:terror-run.text: Terror Run. Terror Run is a perilous swath of land situated in the southwestern reaches of Un'Goro Crater, directly west of the insectoid hives of the Slithering Scar. True to its fearsome name, the territory is stalked by predatory beasts, ranging from massive devilsaurs to ravenous diemetradons and swooping pterrordax. Stretching across the southwestern shelf of Un'Goro Crater, Terror Run lives up to its ominous reputation. Fierce pterrordax wheel through the humid air above while massive diemetradons, stegodons, and apex devilsaurs roam the low brush below. The territory sits directly in the shadow of the mountainous rim, wedged uncomfortably close to the chittering alien mounds of the Slithering Scar. Along the eastern edge of the flats lie the ruined remnants of a camp left behind by Williden Marshal's expedition, a sobering reminder of researchers who were caught unprepared when the crater's primeval predators closed in. Beyond the sheer concentration of hungry fauna, Terror Run draws naturalists and adventurers alike for a geological rarity: it is the primary ground in the crater where curious Red Power Crystals emerge from the fertile soil. The crimson formations hum with primeval energy akin to the blue, green, and yellow crystals found elsewhere in the basin. Surviving long enough to gather them, however, means contending with the sovereign hunters of the plains—including nesting apex devilsaurs that brook no trespassers in the deep south.

subzone:thalassian-base-camp.text: Thalassian Base Camp. Tucked onto a high ridge in northern Azshara, the Thalassian Base Camp serves as the staging ground for an expedition of blood elves unearthing ancient arcane relics. Though initially funded under an agreement with the Horde, the camp's leadership quickly broke faith once digging commenced. Now, amidst their red pavilions and pulverized magical artifacts, darker summoning practices hint at their true objectives. The blood elf expedition nestled east of Ursolan was not supposed to be hostile to travelers from Orgrimmar. Their leader, Magus Rimtori, negotiated a formal pact with the Horde: in exchange for supply lines, funding, and armed escort through Azshara's treacherous wildlands, her researchers would share whatever magical riches they uncovered. Instead, as soon as the base camp was fortified and the first relics were pried from the elven ruins, Rimtori reneged entirely, driving away Horde emissaries. While Rimtori searches deeper reaches with an armed retinue, Magister Hawkhelm keeps watch over the ridge, guarding the encampment against retribution.

subzone:thandol-span.text: Thandol Span. The Thandol Span is a pair of colossal dwarven stone bridges connecting the Wetlands of Khaz Modan with the Arathi Highlands of southern Lordaeron. Long celebrated as a marvel of engineering and the vital artery between the northern and southern kingdoms, it is currently in a state of disaster following a sabotage attack by Dark Iron infiltrators. Constructed following the War of the Three Hammers to bridge Ironforge with the Wildhammer clan of the Aerie Peak, the Thandol Span stands among the grandest stonecraft feats of dwarven history. Capable of supporting entire marching armies, it served as the critical land corridor between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan throughout the Second War, notably carrying Sir Anduin Lothar's counter-offensive southward. Today, the crossing is grievously wounded. Dark Iron saboteurs led by Balgaras the Foul and Kam Deepfury mounted a devastating assault from nearby Dun Modr, shattering one span entirely with explosives and threatening to sever overland travel between the allied realms completely. The surviving bridge remains contested and heavily guarded. Mountaineers from Ironforge fight desperately to preserve the remaining roadway and repel Dark Iron sappers, suffering painful losses in the process. The loss of the bridge would leave northern trade and military movements almost entirely reliant on maritime routes, cutting off Alliance forces stationed across the Arathi Highlands from immediate reinforcement.

subzone:thelgen-rock.text: Thelgen Rock. Thelgen Rock is an extensive cavern system cut into the southern mountain wall of the Wetlands. Infested with venomous spiders, it is notorious for harboring rare veins of volatile Incendicite Ore. Nestled against the southern mountains separating the Wetlands from Loch Modan, Thelgen Rock is a deep subterranean cave network overrun by aggressive arachnids. The passages are thick with webs and crawling with poisonous spiders that make entering the caverns extremely hazardous for travelers. Despite the infestation, miners and adventurers brave its depths for the valuable deposits of Incendicite Ore found embedded in the rocky tunnels.

subzone:theramore-isle.text: Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle is a heavily fortified human port citadel off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Founded by Lady Jaina Proudmoore for refugees escaping the fall of Lordaeron, it stands as the Alliance's primary bastion in southern Kalimdor. Following the devastation of Dalaran and Lordaeron by the Scourge during the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore guided a fleet of survivors across the Great Sea to the shores of Kalimdor. After fighting alongside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal, her coalition of humans, dwarves, and high elves retreated to the misty fringes of Dustwallow Marsh. On a jagged island just off the coast, they built Theramore Isle—a thriving harbor city anchored by towering stone ramparts and Jaina's personal citadel, created to safeguard what remained of the northern kingdoms.

subzone:thistleshrub-valley.text: Thistleshrub Valley. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Tanaris, Thistleshrub Valley is a bizarre oasis of prickly plant life amidst endless dunes. The canyon is known for its strange grove of giant cacti and hostile animated thistleshrubs that attack anything stepping through their thorn-choked territory. While most of Tanaris is an arid wasteland stripped bare of vegetation, Thistleshrub Valley is curiously choked with life. Giant blooming cacti tower over the canyon floor, providing a sharp contrast to the surrounding sea of sand. However, this is no peaceful sanctuary. The valley takes its name from the hostile, living plant creatures that lurk among the brush. These thistleshrubs lash out with razor-sharp spines at any traveler who wanders near, making navigation hazardous for those trying to push past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates. The presence of animated flora in such a dry climate has long puzzled wanderers and desert survivalists. Whether awakened by forgotten elemental energies or stubborn adaptation to the harsh Tanaris climate, the thistleshrubs remain violently territorial. Travelers journeying through the canyon must contend not only with these thrashing thickets of thorn and root, but also the desert predators and venomous serpents that nest among the towering cacti.

subzone:thoradin-s-wall.text: Thoradin's Wall. Thoradin's Wall is a monumental, crumbling stone rampart dividing the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commissioned millennia ago by King Thoradin during the dawn of the Empire of Arathor, it was built to shield early humanity from the fierce incursions of the Amani trolls. Erected nearly three thousand years ago, Thoradin's Wall marks the western frontier of ancient Strom, the heart of the first unified human empire. King Thoradin recognized that humanity's fledgeling settlements were acutely vulnerable to the predatory raids of the Amani forest trolls. By raising this vast stone barrier across the valley corridor, Arathor secured its heartland and forged a defensible bastion from which humanity could survive and eventually contest troll supremacy in the north. Today, the ancient barrier stands in severe disrepair. Vast breeches gash the stone ramparts, their battlements weathered down by thousands of years of exposure, warfare, and abandonment. Following the splintering of Arathor into rival kingdoms and the eventual fall of neighboring Lordaeron to the Scourge, no central realm maintains the masonry. Now, travelers and roaming bandits slip freely through its broken archways as they journey between Hillsbrad and the untamed Arathi Highlands.

subzone:thunder-axe-fortress.text: Thunder Axe Fortress. Thunder Axe Fortress is a fortified compound in northwestern Desolace serving as a stronghold for the demonic Burning Blade cult. Within its stone barracks, watchtowers, and darkened caves, cultists perform dark rituals to summon demonic entities and store stolen artifacts of power. The cult remains an active threat to anyone traversing the desolate wastes. Perched in northwestern Desolace, Thunder Axe Fortress serves as a heavily guarded redoubt for the Burning Blade. Composed of stone barracks, defensive watchtowers, and deep caverns, it allows the cult to maintain a fortified foothold far from the gaze of Kalimdor's major cities. Here, the cultists gather fel energies, summon lesser demons, and concoct schemes to bring far more dangerous entities into the world.

subzone:tidefury-cove.text: Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove is a treacherous stretch of water and rocky shallows along the southeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. Renowned for its hazardous reefs and wrecked vessels, it serves as a secluded haven for roaming makrura and solitary anglers. Tucked away at the far end of Dustwallow Bay between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog, Tidefury Cove presents a notorious navigational hazard to passing sailors. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have claimed multiple vessels over the years, leaving rotting wooden hulks half-submerged in the tideline. Today, the ruined ships are crawled over by opportunistic makrura, turning the cove into a dangerous, isolated stretch of coastline visited mostly by hardy scavengers or quiet hermits seeking distance from Theramore's busy docks. During the invasion of Durotar, the shores of Tidefury Cove became a crucial strategic battleground. Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiran expedition fortified the coast with an imposing coastal fortress and guard towers to command the approaches to Theramore. To break Proudmoore's grip, Thrall marshaled the combined strength of the young Horde—uniting orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren alongside Rexxar and the Stonemaul ogres—to storm the shoreline and dismantle the Kul Tiran beachhead before pressing directly toward the island fortress.

subzone:tkashi-ruins.text: Tkashi Ruins. The Tkashi Ruins are ancient stone remnants situated southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Overrun by hostile Bloodscalp trolls, the site remains a stronghold of the tribe. Perched southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, the crumbling stone masonry of the Tkashi Ruins marks the ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. Today, the encampment is heavily occupied by the Bloodscalp tribe, who aggressively defend the territory and practice their shamanistic rituals among the vines and decayed stone. While Hemet Nesingwary noted passing through the ruins without trouble in his hunting memoirs, modern travelers find the trolls far less accommodating, guarding valuable tribal relics buried among the rubble.

subzone:tower-of-arathor.text: Tower of Arathor. The Tower of Arathor is a ruined wizard's tower situated in the former mage district in the southwestern reaches of Stromgarde Keep. Once the workshop of Archmage Trelane, it was overrun during the fall of the city and is currently occupied by Boulderfist ogres. Erected in the heart of Stromgarde Keep's mage district and named after the ancient Empire of Arathor, this spire long served the realm's sorcerers. Its most notable resident, Archmage Trelane, devised a magical defensive grid keyed to enchanted gemstones to protect the sanctum. However, when the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogre clan assaulted Stromgarde following the Third War, the kingdom fractured. Despite Trelane's desperate attempts to hold the tower using his arcane wards, the sheer brutish force of the ogres overwhelmed him. Forced to flee the city for his life, the archmage left behind his most prized arcane artifacts, leaving the spire in the hands of the Boulderfist brute Ruul Onestone and his followers.

subzone:tower-of-eldara.text: Tower of Eldara. The Tower of Eldara is an ancient, sealed night elven spire situated on the far northeastern promontory overlooking the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Though long abandoned, its sturdy stone architecture has survived the Sundering, standing silent above coasts roamed by aggressive coastal beasts. Perched on a remote cliff edge northeast of the Bay of Storms, the Tower of Eldara stands as a lonely testament to the vast kaldorei empire that once dominated this coastline. Like much of Azshara's ruined architecture, it fell into disuse following the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Today, the entrance remains firmly closed and barred against the outside world, giving no hint of whatever relics or chambers lie sealed inside. The surrounding shores are fraught with danger, prowled constantly by wandering murlocs, clawing makrura, and predatory hydras that keep all but the most daring travelers away.

subzone:twin-colossals.text: Twin Colossals. The Twin Colossals are a pair of towering, sheer-faced mesas that dominate the northwestern skyline of Feralas. Rising high above the canopy, the narrow passage between their sheer cliffs forms the primary overland route connecting Feralas with the arid wastes of Desolace to the north. Towering over the western reaches of Feralas, the Twin Colossals stand as the highest landforms in the region. Their vertical rock faces cut a striking silhouette against the sky, serving as unmistakable landmarks for travelers venturing south out of Desolace. While the lower slopes merge into the dense jungle and the lands stretching toward the Forgotten Coast, the summits are isolated plateaus far above the forest floor. Scaling the vertical cliffs on foot is impossible, yet the summits are not entirely deserted. An intrepid night elf named Marli Wishrunner assists travelers seeking passage to the eastern peak. Those who ascend find a tranquil pond perched atop the stone mesa—though it is inhabited by an unusually large makrura named Diamond Head. To aid adventurers in returning to earth, Kalin Windflight offers sturdy parachutes to descend back into the jungle canopy below.

subzone:uldum.text: Uldum. Uldum is a massive, sealed Titan research installation tucked behind colossal stone gates in the southernmost cliffs of Tanaris. Long hidden away behind ancient wards and forgotten machinery, it remains inaccessible to modern explorers. Carved into the rugged southern mountain range bordering the Tanaris desert, the monumental gateway to Uldum stands silent and impassable. Built during the ordering of ancient Kalimdor, the compound served as an advanced Titan facility tied to their mysterious efforts to shape and oversee the planet's biosphere. Titanic wardens and defensive constructs once maintained the perimeter, leaving modern mortals only monumental stone carved arches and buried secrets that have defied all mundane attempts at entry. The site's unmistakable Titan craftsmanship draws the curiosity of dwarven scholars, yet no mechanism or key has been found that might unlock the ancient complex. Legend claims that true insight into the secrets locked within requires the lost Plates of Uldum, leaving the dwarven scholars peering through the keyhole of an empire they cannot yet breach.

subzone:uplands.text: Uplands. The Uplands is a rolling, elevated territory in the northeastern Alterac Mountains that once served as the agricultural heartland of the fallen Kingdom of Alterac. Following the kingdom's collapse, the fertile hills fell entirely under the sway of the Syndicate. Today, the criminal organization maintains its strongest base of power here, fortifying multiple encampments across the slopes. Before the Second War broke Alterac apart, the hills of the Uplands were celebrated as the kingdom's breadbasket, providing grain and livestock to feed its mountain fortresses. When the core of the realm fell to ruin and infamy, the farming estates were abandoned by honest folk. In their place rose the Syndicate, led by dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats determined to reclaim their stolen inheritance through force. The Uplands now represents the Syndicate's most heavily concentrated territory in the region, dotted with camps, patrols, and outposts like Dandred's Fold along its western borders. Because the Syndicate commands these hills in force, high-ranking conspirators often oversee operations from the Uplands. Figures such as Baron Vardus, aligned with the shadowy leadership steering the remnants of Alterac's nobility, coordinate brigand movements, raids on neighboring valleys, and resistance against both the Alliance and Horde. Travelers crossing into the northeastern ridges face immediate hostility from entrenched highwaymen who view the entire range as their sovereign soil.

subzone:ursolan.text: Ursolan. Ursolan is a sprawling Timbermaw furbolg settlement situated in western Azshara, just east of Timbermaw Hold. Bisected by a deep ravine, the encampment honors the bear Ancient Ursol and serves as a vital stronghold for uncorrupted furbolgs defending their territory from outside incursions. Perched on the rugged bluffs of western Azshara, Ursolan constitutes the eastern branch of the Timbermaw tribe's domain, connecting directly through Timbermaw Hold to Bear's Head in the south. Named after the revered bear Ancient Ursol, this camp represents a rare haven of sanity among Kalimdor's furbolg populations, which have largely fallen victim to demonic corruption. The village spans both rims of a dramatic earthen chasm, where the Timbermaw vigilantly guard their borders against encroaching interlopers, including intrusive researchers from the night elven camp of Talrendis.

subzone:valley-of-bones.text: Valley of Bones. The Valley of Bones is a desolate canyon along the crags of Shen'dralas, choked with dust, ancient remains, and restless undead. Haunted by the lingering spirits of the Magram centaur clan and patrolled by dark necromancers, it is dominated by the colossal rib cages of mysterious ancient beasts known as the Dead Goliaths. Tucked away in the southern reaches of the region, the Valley of Bones lives up to its grim name. Skeletal horrors walk the dusty ravines, raised and bound by centaur necromancers who draw upon dark sorceries. The spirits of deceased Magram centaur wander the wastes alongside them, bound to this barren earth long after their violent deaths. Adding to the canyon's ominous nature are the Dead Goliaths—two immense skeletons slumped against the rocky cliffs whose true origin remains a total mystery to scholars and wanderers alike.

subzone:valley-of-fangs.text: Valley of Fangs. The Valley of Fangs is a rugged, narrow pass carved between towering rock pillars in the central Badlands. Known for the vicious predators that prowl its dusty floor, it also shelters a small, isolated encampment of wandering tinkerers and exiles. Situated between two imposing stone formations in the heart of the Badlands, the Valley of Fangs earns its name from both the sharp silhouettes of its surrounding cliffs and the dangerous beasts roaming its floor. Feral crag coyotes, prowling cougars, and vicious wolves stalk the dusty corridor, making transit hazardous for lone travelers. Despite the hostile wildlife, a handful of wayward figures—including the banished orc Martek the Exiled and his goblin associates Rigglefuzz and Jazzrik—have pitched an informal camp here, tinkering away in seclusion far from the regional outposts.

subzone:valley-of-spears.text: Valley of Spears. The Valley of Spears is a rugged canyon nestled in western Desolace, serving as the stronghold of the Maraudine centaur clan. Enclosed by steep cliffs and guarded passes, the valley leads directly to Maraudon, the sacred ancestral burial ground of all centaurkind. Carved into the rugged heights of western Desolace, the Valley of Spears is a stronghold of the Maraudine clan. Accessible on foot only through narrow, easily defended mountain passes from the south and east, this enclosed valley provides the centaur with a natural bastion. Travelers who venture past the rocky chokepoints face dense encampments of hostile nomads guarding the approach to their most revered holy site. Tucked away at the southwestern end of the valley lies the entrance to Maraudon, the sacred cavern housing the tomb of Zaetar, father of the centaur, where Princess Theradras dwells. Because of this proximity, the Maraudine defend the canyon with zealous fury against rival clans and outside interlopers alike. Anyone foolish enough to stumble into the valley unawares—such as careless gnome cartographers or scouts—frequently ends up captured or slain.

subzone:valley-of-the-watchers.text: Valley of the Watchers. Tucked away in the far southern reaches of the Tanaris desert, the Valley of the Watchers is a sun-scorched canyon defined by monumental stonework. At its end stands a colossal, sealed stone gate leading into the mysterious complex of Uldum, guarded by lumbering giants and ancient stone sentinels. The Valley of the Watchers marks the southern boundary where the shifting sands of Tanaris meet the mountainous edge of the continent. Dominating the canyon is a massive gate crafted from ancient stone, locked tight against the outside world. This sealed portal is believed to guard the entrance to Uldum, a subterranean facility of the enigmatic Titans. Massive Dune Smasher mountain giants roam the dusty approach, ensuring that whatever secrets lie buried beneath the sands remain undisturbed by travelers, tomb robbers, and scholars alike.

subzone:valormok.text: Valormok. Valormok is a remote Horde outpost established in the rugged northwest reaches of Azshara. Positioned north of the Haldarr Encampment, this windswept settlement serves as a staging ground for scouts and adventurers braving the cursed, ancient ruins of the coast. Perched among the autumn-colored trees of Azshara, Valormok represents the Horde's tentative interest in a hostile and largely forsaken territory. Life here is bleak and fraught with peril; the camp is lightly fortified and constantly exposed to nearby satyrs, nagas, and prowling beasts. Despite these hardships, its stationed warriors hold the ground, acting as a crucial flight hub and forward bastion connecting Orgrimmar with the wilder stretches of northern Kalimdor.

subzone:venture-co-base-camp.text: Venture Co. Base Camp. Tucked away in the dense jungles of northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Venture Co. Base Camp serves as a forward foothold for the notoriously greedy goblin syndicate. Here, hired overseers and laborers exploit the lush wilderness, focusing their efforts on harvesting timber, hunting local wildlife, and extracting valuable tumbled crystals from the nearby waterways. The Venture Company is infamous across Azeroth for ruthless profiteering and complete disregard for the natural world. At this jungle base camp, steam-powered equipment and makeshift goblin shacks chew into the ancient canopy. Guarded by armed mercenaries, foremen, and field workers, the camp coordinates resource extraction throughout the surrounding valleys, paying particular interest to valuable tumbled crystals found nearby while clear-cutting any jungle that stands in their way.

subzone:vile-reef.text: Vile Reef. The Vile Reef is a submerged, vibrant coral shelf lying off the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale near Grom'gol Base Camp. Beneath its waters, aggressive murlocs make their home among ancient sunken troll ruins, giant clams, and coastal shipwrecks. Stretching beneath the waves of the Great Sea just offshore from Grom'gol Base Camp, the Vile Reef is known for its vivid marine growth and perilous inhabitants. The seabed is dotted with the weathered stonework of submerged troll ruins alongside the enigmatic Altar of the Tides. Flocks of territorial murlocs lurk among the coral shelves and shattered timbers of passing vessels, fiercely defending the shallow waters and preying upon any diver who braves the deep in search of giant clams and rare blue pearls.

subzone:warpwood-quarter.text: Warpwood Quarter. The Warpwood Quarter encompasses the eastern district of the ruined Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Once a center of elven nature cultivation and lush gardens, it has devolved into a warped, demon-tainted ruin overrun by frenzied flora and corrupted satyrs. Formerly known for its grand botanical marvels, the Warpwood Quarter has become a choking forest of twisted ancients and lethal lashers. The district fell under the sway of Alzzin the Wildshaper, a satyr who bent his dark magic toward defiling the ancient Fruit of Fertility. Under his malign influence, the plant life grew grotesque and predatory, saturating the halls with vile Felvine shards and drawing demons, rebellious imps, and demonic thralls into the ruined halls. While explorers typically enter the district through the central Broken Commons of Dire Maul, an overgrown subterranean backdoor lies hidden beneath the Lariss Pavilion to the east. Navigating the district requires contending not only with Alzzin's warped guardians, but also with elusive denizens such as the mischievous imp Pusillin, whose thievery leads pursuers on dangerous chases toward the secluded reaches of the ruins.

subzone:waterspring-field.text: Waterspring Field. Waterspring Field is a vital water-pumping operation in northern Tanaris, constructed by the goblins of Gadgetzan to tap underground aquifers. Instead of supplying the boomtown, the field has been overtaken by the ruthless Wastewander bandits, who now hoard the desert's most precious resource. In the searing wastes of Tanaris, nothing carries more value than fresh water. Seeking to support their expanding trade hub, the Steamwheedle Cartel goblins of Gadgetzan erected an array of industrial pumping towers across Waterspring Field to draw from underground reserves. Their plans collapsed when the Wastewanders—a sprawling band of human outlaws and desert marauders—seized the entire field. The bandits now guard the hijacked pumps with their lives, forcing Gadgetzan to look for hired blades willing to reclaim the moisture.

subzone:weazel-s-crater.text: Weazel's Crater. Weazel's Crater is a deep gouge carved into the hard salt of the northern Shimmering Flats. Its origins are mysterious, and Saltstone basilisks inhabit the hollow. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, experimental goblin and gnome rocket-cars constantly push the boundaries of mechanical sanity. Debris, scorched earth, and impact hollows litter the plains, but Weazel's Crater stands out for its sheer size and depth. The crater's origins are unknown. Today, the mechanical wreckage has largely settled, and the hollow has been claimed as a sunning pit by aggressive Saltstone basilisks.

subzone:whispering-gardens.text: Whispering Gardens. The Whispering Gardens occupy the terraced hillside just south of the Scarlet Monastery in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a place of quiet contemplation, it became the site of a savage clash between early crusade defenders and a massive host of the Scourge. Today, crusaders patrol its overgrown pathways while the faint voices of the fallen linger in the air. Before the Scarlet Crusade fully retreated behind the fortress walls of the Monastery, a fierce battle erupted across these terraced slopes against an encroaching army of undead. The clash claimed countless lives on both sides. In the twilight, travelers through the gardens report hearing strange, soft murmurings on the wind—believed to be the restless echoes of the soldiers and priests who perished defending the holy grounds. Despite the haunting presence, the Scarlet Crusade maintains an active watch over the gardens. Scarlet scouts, magicians, and preservers guard the trails to intercept any intruders approaching from the lower glades. For the zealots within the nearby monastery, these overgrown steps serve as both a defensive bulwark and a solemn reminder of the ceaseless war against the undead.

subzone:wild-shore.text: Wild Shore. The Wild Shore is the southernmost coastline of Stranglethorn Vale, where the jungle meets the waves of the South Seas. It serves as a staging ground and anchorage for the Bloodsail Buccaneers, whose ships lie moored along the shallows. Stretching along the bottom tip of the continent, the Wild Shore marks the border where Stranglethorn Vale plunges into the South Seas. To the northwest lies the fortified inlet of Booty Bay, while a shallow ocean strait separates the mainland beach from Jaguero Isle to the east.
